Title: Rauf says people interests come first in Melaka political cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the interests of the state and its people would take precedence in any political cooperation.
"Let us settle this (the dissolution) first. After that, we will talk about the party and where we are heading.
"Certainly, I will have negotiations with any parties involved and will assess our discussions and the offers that are made.
"Most importantly, it is not about my interests, but about how we are going to administer this state for the people," he told a press conference at Kompleks Seri Negeri.
Rauf was responding to a question on possible cooperation under BN Plus, as he had announced on Aug 2.
Earlier, Rauf announced that the Melaka state assembly would be dissolved tomorrow.
He said Yang di-Pertua Negeri Melaka Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam had consented to the dissolution.
Rauf previously said that the momentum generated by the understanding between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional in the Negri Sembilan state election had paved the way for the emergence of "BN Plus" in Melaka.
Rauf, who is BN chairman, said the BN Plus approach provided room for all parties to engage in discussions, but any decision would be based on BN's interests and strength in the state.
He said no coalition had been officially finalised so far and Melaka BN was not bound by any form of political cooperation with other parties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 11 hurt as teen opens fire outside Turkiye school
Article:
TURGUTLU: A teenager opened fire outside a high school in western Turkiye on Tuesday, wounding 11 people before being detained by police, a minister said.
The incident happened around 8am (0500 GMT) in Turgutlu in Manisa province, near the western resort city of Izmir, the regional governor's office said.
School shootings are rare in Turkiye, although there were two attacks in April on consecutive days in southern Turkiye that sparked widespread anger.
"Eleven students were injured, two of them seriously.. The minor who carried out the attack was quickly apprehended and taken into custody," Justice Minister Akin Gurlek wrote on X.
He said the suspect's parents and grandfather had also been detained by investigators probing the attack, which saw police and rescuers rushing to the scene alongside panicked parents.
DHA news agency broadcast CCTV footage of the alleged attacker, a young man wearing black jeans, a black jacket and a green top walking along a street holding what appeared to be a long-barrelled gun.
IHA had a similar image of what appeared to be the same person with a gun, although this time running.
NTV private television said it was a shotgun.
Footage from outside the school showed police wrestling a man in a white shirt to the ground before leading him away, as a woman screamed, with onlookers pressed against the school fence, filming with their mobile phones.
Authorities have opened an investigation into the incident, Gurlek said.
"How the weapon used in the attack ended up in the minor's hands, the conditions under which it was kept and supervised.. and allegations of bullying prior to the incident are all being investigated," he wrote on X.
The education ministry said all lessons were suspended for the day at the school.
- SCHOOL SAFETY -
The attack came five months after two back-to-back school shootings that raised public concerns about security in Turkish schools.
In April, a 14-year-old opened fire at a school in the southern province of Kahramanmaras, killing a teacher and nine students aged 10 and 11. The attacker died at the scene.
A day earlier, another teenager opened fire at his former high school in the southeastern province of Sanliurfa, wounding 16 people before taking his own life when confronted by police.
Following the two attacks, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan dismissed a deputy education minister and pledged his government would introduce tighter controls on gun ownership.
He vowed school safety would be one of the government's top priorities.
"When we look at similar attacks around the world, especially in the United States, we see one of the perpetrators' aims is to terrorise society," he said.
- NEW SECURITY MEASURES -
The attack came a day after Education Minister Yusuf Tekin and Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci signed a protocol setting out security measures for the 2026-2027 academic year, which began on Sept 14.
He said 31,000 school grounds supervisors had been deployed for the first time.
The ministry also carried out a fresh security assessment of schools and assigned police officers to first- and second-degree risk schools, where they remain on permanent duty, he said.
Schools classified as lower risk are assigned police liaison officers who work in coordination with school administrations.--AFP

Title: Van driver fined RM12,000 for abusing two stepchildren with pestle, iron
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A tourist van driver broke down in tears in the dock and pleaded for leniency after admitting to abusing his two stepchildren with a pestle and an iron last August.
Sessions Court judge Suhaila Haron fined Joharis Mahmod, 48, RM12,000 for two counts of abusing the boys aged 17 and 9.
She ordered Joharis to serve five months in jail if he fails to pay the fine.
She also ordered him to perform 72 hours of community service within six months and placed him under a two-year good-behaviour bond of RM2,000 with one surety.
Joharis pleaded guilty to two charges of abusing his stepchildren and causing them injuries at an apartment unit in Pudu Impian 2, Cheras, at 10.30pm on Aug 13.
The charges framed under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 carries a maximum fine of RM50,000, jail for up to 20 years, or both upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case, a schoolteacher lodged a complaint after noticing physical injuries on the children's bodies.
An investigation was conducted, leading to Joharis' arrest.
Police also seized a stone mortar and pestle and an iron believed to have been used in the incident.
Investigations found that Joharis had slapped the younger child's cheeks five times and beaten the older child with a pestle and an iron.
Medical reports confirmed that the younger child suffered bruising on both cheeks while the older child sustained multiple bruises to the back and scalp.
Deputy public prosecutor Md Subri Hashim urged the court to impose a proportionate sentence on Joharis as a deterrent and to send a clear message to the public.
He said parents had a responsibility to care for the children entrusted to them.
In mitigation, Joharis, who was unrepresented by counsel, appealed for a lighter sentence and promised not to repeat the offence.
He said he was the sole breadwinner for his family, supporting his unemployed wife and five stepchildren.

Title: BigBang KL concert tickets snapped up in under 5 minutes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tickets for BigBang's Kuala Lumpur concert sold out in less than 5 minutes during the general sale today, leaving thousands of fans scrambling for seats to the highly anticipated show.
The overwhelming demand has prompted fans who missed the official sale to turn to social media in search of tickets, while some existing ticket holders have also begun offering theirs for resale.
While some are genuinely looking to pass on tickets they no longer need, others are allegedly taking advantage of the high demand to target desperate fans looking for seats.
A fan who wanted to be known as Cayden said he was allegedly scammed of RM1,800 while attempting to buy two tickets from a reseller he met through Threads.
He said the individual approached him through his Threads post after he indicated that he was looking for tickets to the concert.
"I checked his Touch 'n Go name, Truecaller and the name linked to his Wise bank account.
"He also provided an email confirmation of the tickets, which appeared legitimate, and I had seen the ticket confirmation on his Instagram Story," he said.
Cayden said he made the full payment before the seller asked him to wait 5 minutes while he changed the email address and identification details linked to the tickets.
"After that, he blocked me on all my social media accounts and my phone number. I could no longer contact him," he said, adding that he planned to lodge a police report.
Another fan, Mikhail Hansnor Mohd Hajmi, 22, said he failed to secure tickets despite preparing two devices and joining the online queue at about 9.30am.
He said he managed to enter the ticketing platform at exactly 10am but encountered a transaction cancellation when he reached the payment stage.
However, Nur Arina Shahirah Sharudin, 29, said she used a ticketing service after having no previous experience buying tickets for a major concert.
She said the service helped her secure 2 tickets during the V.I.P. membership presale, with confirmation from Fantopia received at about 10.07am on Sept 17.
The BigBang 2026-2027 World Tour Kuala Lumpur concert is scheduled for Jan 9 next year at Stadium Nasional Bukit Jalil.
iMe Malaysia, in a comment on its post, said Fantopia is the only official ticketing platform for the BigBang KL concert.
"Please do not purchase tickets from any other unofficial or unrelated websites or platforms," it added.

Title: [UPDATED] Negri Sembilan MB suspends two top state officials
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan government has suspended state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal with immediate effect, Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said today.
In a statement, Ismail said the decision was made unanimously at a special meeting of the state executive council (MMKN) today.
He said state financial officer Datuk Masri Razali would perform the duties of state secretary until a new state secretary is appointed by the Chief Secretary to the Government.
Meanwhile, lawyer Fahmi Adilah will provide legal advice until a new state legal adviser is appointed by the Attorney General's Chambers, he said.
Ismail said notice of Zafir's suspension would be conveyed to the Chief Secretary to the Government and the Public Service Department, while notice of Muzalmah's suspension would be conveyed to the Attorney General's Chambers.
He also confirmed that all state executive council members remained in their positions.
"At the same time, the Negri Sembilan government administration will continue to function as usual, and its responsibilities to the people will continue to be carried out to the best of its ability," he said.
The announcement comes amid an ongoing dispute over the status of the Negri Sembilan state executive council.
On Sunday, the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, revoked the appointments of the state executive council members with immediate effect.
The Istana said the decision was made after the exco members were found to have violated their oath of office through their actions and statements on Sept 15.
However, Ismail has maintained that the exco members remain in office and will continue carrying out their duties.
He said any action to dismiss or terminate an exco member without the advice or request of the Menteri Besar constituted a legal error and had no legal force.

Title: URTI, asthma, conjunctivitis cases decline amid persistent haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis cases have declined, but the Health Ministry has urged the public to continue taking precautions as the haze persists.
The ministry said the haze affecting several parts of the country had entered its seventh week, while surveillance at 78 designated health facilities nationwide showed a decline in all three haze-related illnesses in epidemiological week (ME) 37/2026 compared with ME 36/2026.
It said URTI cases had fallen by 20.18 per cent, from 7,065 to 5,639– a decrease of 1,426 cases.
Asthma cases dropped by 35.36 per cent, from 1,117 to 722, while conjunctivitis cases declined by 32.04 per cent, from 334 to 227.
"Despite the decline in the haze-related illnesses being monitored, the ministry will continue to closely monitor the haze situation and its impact on health, particularly in areas recording unhealthy air quality," it said in a statement today.
The ministry advised the public to postpone strenuous outdoor activities and reduce time spent outdoors during hazy conditions, particularly children, the elderly and those with chronic respiratory or heart conditions.
The ministry warned those who need to go outdoors to limit their time outside and wear suitable face masks in affected areas.
People with chronic respiratory or heart conditions should continue taking medication as prescribed, while those who develop symptoms or whose condition worsens should seek treatment at the nearest health facility.
The ministry has implemented several measures to monitor the haze and protect public health, including activating the National Haze Operations Room on Sept 4 to coordinate monitoring and response efforts.
URTI, asthma and conjunctivitis cases are also monitored daily through the 78 designated health facilities and assessing air quality readings alongside health surveillance data to determine appropriate public health measures.
Health facilities have been prepared with adequate medicines, oxygen supplies and related medical equipment, while health education, risk communication and public health advisories have been stepped up, particularly for high-risk groups.
As of this morning,
10 areas in Sarawak
continued to dominate unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, while four others were recorded in Putrajaya, Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Sabah.
Another 51 areas recorded moderate air quality, while three were at good levels.

Title: Singapore online safety commission receives over 500 reports in first two months
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore's Online Safety Commission (OSC) received more than 500 reports of online harm in its first two months of operation, resolving over 90 per cent of eligible cases.
Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo said the figures covered reports received between June 29 and Aug 31 this year.
"The bulk of them are doxxing and online harassment, with a far smaller proportion involving intimate image abuse and online stalking," she said on the "Let's Table It" podcast aired on the gov.sg YouTube channel on Tuesday.
According to OSC data, doxxing accounted for the largest share of reports at 44 per cent, followed by online harassment (38 per cent), intimate image abuse (eight per cent), online stalking (seven per cent) and image-based child abuse (three per cent).
The commission said victims aged 18 and below were involved in 17 per cent of all eligible reports.
The youngest victim was seven years old and involved in a doxxing case, while the oldest was 68 and subjected to online harassment.
Meanwhile, Commissioner of Online Safety Francis Ng said each report received by the OSC would be assigned to a case officer to assess whether all requirements for action had been met.
The commission would then contact the relevant online platform to seek further action.
"We typically start by giving the platwads-up, what we call a flag. Very often, these flags are enough to get the platforms to move and remove the content.
"Thereafter, we might, if we need to, follow up with a direction that is basically a legal notice that goes to the platform and tells the platform, you have to access disable or block the content," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Scheduled water disruption in Seremban, Rembau, PD until Thursday
Article:
SEREMBAN: Consumers in parts of Seremban, Rembau and Port Dickson will experience a scheduled water supply disruption from today until Thursday due to maintenance works at the Sungai Terip and Sawah Raja water treatment plants (WTPs).
Syarikat Air Negri Sembilan Sdn Bhd (SAINS), in a Facebook post today, said the affected areas in Seremban include Senawang, Rasah, Rahang, Ampangan, Seremban 2 and Sikamat.
In Rembau, the disruption affects Kampung Kundur Hilir, Taman Akasia Kundur, Exevalley Orchard Park, Pengkalan Durian, Kampung Sungai Radin, Kampung Sungai Timun Dalam and Kampung Sungai Timun Luar.
Meanwhile, affected areas in Port Dickson include Ladang Tampin Linggi, the entire Linggi area, Pengkalan Kempas and the Port Dickson Hospital.
SAINS said the maintenance involves pipe and valve connections, valve replacements and scheduled electrical system servicing.
As of noon today, work progress at the Sungai Terip WTP had reached 55 per cent, while the Sawah Raja WTP was at 35 per cent.
SAINS said water supply will be restored in stages once the on-site works are fully completed, although high-lying areas and those at the end of the distribution system may experience a longer recovery period.
The company has also prepared water tankers and static tanks as a contingency measure should the disruption extend beyond 42 hours.
Consumers can contact the SAINS Customer Service Centre at 1-300-88-6982 for more information and emergency water assistance throughout the disruption period.

Title: BHESS, EC start engagement on increasing Sabah and Sarawak parliamentary seats
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah and Sarawak Affairs Division (BHESS) of the Prime Minister's Department has initiated engagement with the Election Commission (EC) to discuss the direction and implementation mechanism for the proposal to increase the number of members of parliament (MPs) from Sabah and Sarawak.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said he led BHESS on a courtesy call to EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun today to discuss the matter.
He said the meeting followed developments at the federal government level, including the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63) meeting on Sept 11, which acknowledged that the matter had been discussed during the cabinet meeting.
Mustapha said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also expressed that there was justification for increasing the ratio of MPs from Sabah and Sarawak, subject to further discussions with EC.
"Currently, Sabah and Sarawak hold 56 seats, or 25.3 per cent of the total seats in the Dewan Rakyat. The proposal put forward is to bring the total to 35 per cent, balanced against the seats in Peninsular Malaysia," he said in a statement today.
He said today's discussions also focused on the processes and the constitutional, legal, and technical considerations including aspects of electoral boundary delineation, required data, and the nature of engagement between the government, the EC, and stakeholders.
"This is not merely a question of adding seats. It is about ensuring that the standing and voices of Sabah and Sarawak in Parliament continue to be strengthened, in line with the original spirit of the formation of Malaysia and the implementation of MA63," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MQA calls for structured drone training at higher education institutions
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA) chief executive officer Datuk Prof Mohamad Shatar Sabran has called for structured drone operation training to be organised by higher education institutions.
He said that most drone operators, particularly in rural areas, acquire their skills independently rather than through formal instruction.
"Drone operation has been identified as a high-impact emerging skill that warrants formal training recognition, in line with the shift in the country's higher education landscape towards alternative learning pathways through micro-credential programmes," he said in a statement today.
As a way forward, he said individuals intending to operate drones are expected to hold a certification recognised by an authoritative body.
In this regard, he said those interested can now enrol in short drone operation courses at universities with MQA verification and accreditation through the Quality Verification Centre.
"Overall, this micro-credential initiative offers flexible pathways for upskilling and reskilling across all segments of society," he said.
He said that this alternative approach provides a second chance for those who are unable to pursue conventional studies to obtain an academic qualification certificate.
He said the Higher Education Ministry is now encouraging all local higher education institutions to roll out specialised skills-based programmes such as drone operation more aggressively.
"This is important to enable these institutions to make full use of available capacity to produce recognised skilled workers.
"Their active involvement will indirectly ensure that the country's future workforce needs and challenges are addressed effectively from now on," he said. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man jailed 10 years, six strokes over sexual offences against teenage girlfriend
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A man who checked into a motel twice with his teenage girlfriend was sentenced to 10 years in jail and six strokes of the rotan for raping and sexually assaulting the girl.
Sessions Court Judge Monica Linsua handed down the sentences to Mohd Ashriff Haikal Samlli, 24, after he pleaded guilty to all four charges today.
On the first charge, Mohd Ashriff was sentenced to nine years in jail and two strokes of the rotan for raping the girl, who was then 15 years and seven months old, in a motel room in Sipitang on Jan 23.
He was sentenced to 10 years in jail and two strokes of the rotan on the second charge of raping the same girl at the same motel on March 24.
For the third charge, he was sentenced to six years in jail and one stroke of the rotan for sexually assaulting the girl at the same place on Jan 23.
On the fourth charge, he was sentenced to seven years in jail and one stroke of the rotan for committing the same offence against the girl on March 24.
The court ordered all the jail terms to run concurrently from the date of his arrest on March 26. This means he will serve a total of 10 years in jail, rather than 32 years, and receive six strokes of the rotan.
For the rape charges, Mohd Ashriff was convicted under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping.
For the sexual assault charges, he was convicted under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping.
According to the facts of the case, the girl's mother lodged a police report on March 25 after discovering that her daughter had been away from home between 2pm and 8pm the previous day.
When the girl returned home, her mother noticed a red mark on her neck. The girl subsequently disclosed that she had had sexual intercourse with Mohd Ashriff, who was her boyfriend.
On March 26, the girl was examined by an obstetrics and gynaecology specialist, who confirmed old tears in her hymen at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions, as well as bruising on the left side of her neck.
In mitigation, Mohd Ashriff, who was unrepresented, pleaded for leniency and asked not to be imprisoned, saying what happened was a mistake and that he had no malicious intent.
He also told the court that both his parents were fully dependent on him and that imprisonment would cause him to lose his job and the income he used to support them.
Deputy public prosecutor Fazriel Fardiansyah Abdul Kadir, however, pressed for a deterrent sentence, citing the seriousness of the offences and the victim's young age.
He submitted that at 15, the victim was emotionally, physically and psychologically immature and incapable of fully understanding the gravity of the acts committed against her or protecting herself from an adult perpetrator.
Fazriel also stressed that the offences were not committed on a single occasion but on two separate dates.
The prosecution submitted that the repeated offences against the same victim demonstrated a deliberate and repetitive pattern of behaviour and sought a lengthy custodial sentence as a deterrent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Student opens fire outside school in Turkiye, eight pupils wounded, NTV reports
Article:
ANKARA: A student opened fire in front of their high school in Turkiye's western province of Manisa on Tuesday, wounding at least eight other pupils, broadcaster NTV reported.
Two of the wounded were in a critical condition, NTV said. The assailant was caught, the local governor's office said.
"A report was received regarding gunfire in the vicinity of the Inci Uzmez Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School in our Turgutlu district at 7.59 (0459 GMT)," the office added on X.
Images and video posted online showed a male figure walking on a street near the school with a rifle in his hands.
He was then seen running back from the same street.
The motive for the attack was not immediately clear.
Two deadly school shootings in April caused outrage in Turkiye and prompted officials to bring in new security measures for the 2026-2027 academic year, including tighter gun controls.
Before then, the country had not had a history of such attacks.
Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz said Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci and Education Minister Yusuf Tekin were going to Manisa to carry out inspections.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's rainy season delayed to November as El Nino persists
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia is expected to experience a shorter than usual rainy season this year starting in November, the weather agency said on Tuesday, with the El Nino weather pattern to last until the first quarter of 2027.
The agency previously forecast it would come in October, when the wet season usually starts. About 61 per cent of Indonesia's land area will experience the delayed rainy season, agency chief Teuku Faisal Fathani told a press conference.
The wet season is estimated to come early November in most areas of Indonesia including some parts of Kalimantan and the islands of Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi, Teuku said.
The extended dry season had contributed to Indonesia's most intense wildfires in 11 years as "super El Nino" weather drives up temperatures and causes droughts.
Fires burned 202,000ha of land between January and July, official figures show, while environmental group YKAN estimates an additional 600,000ha were affected in August.
The weather agency advised the food sector to adjust planting schedules and choose crop varieties with shorter growing cycles to anticipate the prolonged dry season.
The wet season will peak in most parts of Indonesia in December, with heavy rain still likely in January and February next year.
The El Nino weather pattern was still having a strong impact in most parts of Indonesia during September, another official Ardhasena Sopaheluwakan said, adding the phenomenon is estimated to last until the first quarter but its impact on drought will end when the wet season comes.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rauf: Thank you, Melaka people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh today thanked the people of the state as the legislative assembly is set to be dissolved tomorrow.
"Thank you to the people of Melaka. We (the state executive councillors) have worked together for the people.
Melaka Sayang Rakyat
," he said at a press conference in Seri Negeri where he announced the upcoming dissolution.
He said Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam had
consented to the dissolution
.
The move ends weeks of speculation over when the state assembly would be dissolved.
Meanwhile, when asked about the performance of his state executive council, Rauf expressed his appreciation for the cooperation of its members and government agencies in serving the people.
"This was particularly evident in our efforts to reach out to the people through the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat programme, followed by the Hari Exco Bertemu Rakyat programme."
Rauf, who is the Tanjung Bidara assemblyman, said the programmes had enabled the state administration to resolve more than 5,000 complaints across the state.
"About 80 per cent have been successfully resolved, involving various issues such as welfare, healthcare, schools, drains and street lights. You name it, we have dealt with them.
"For the remainder, we are conducting assessments and studies on how assistance can be channelled, whether by referring the matters to the federal government or resolving them individually through the appropriate channels.
"So, if you ask me, I am very satisfied with all the elected representatives who have provided the best service to the people of Melaka under the 'Melaka Sayang Rakyat' concept," he said.
Rauf said the programmes carried out during his tenure as chief minister had also enabled the state government to identify issues that had previously not reached his attention.
"I have made the elected representatives in their respective areas the eyes, ears and voice of the state administration, allowing us to identify and resolve issues on the ground."
Asked whether the programmes would continue under a new framework if the government was given another mandate, Rauf said the initiative would continue as it was an effective way of reaching out to the people.
"We will continue this effort because I think this is a very good instrument for us to reach out to the people.
"Going out to meet the people takes three years, not two months. It is not just one round from the first N01 state constituency to the last state constituency. It takes three years to complete the entire round.
"Certainly, the response is different from the first day until now. At the beginning, they did not realise that this was the best instrument for the government to reach out to the people and address their needs from various angles."

Title: Philippine bus operators press Marcos for fare hike as fuel costs soar
Article:
MANILA: Philippine bus operators pressed President Ferdinand Marcos on Tuesday to let them raise ticket prices, arguing that soaring fuel costs from the Middle East war threatened to make operations "impossible."
The cost of diesel, which powers most of the Southeast Asian country's buses, has effectively doubled since the first US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February triggered the conflict.
The Philippine transport board approved a fare hike in March, only for Marcos to quash the move a day later.
Ticket prices have remained static ever since.
On Tuesday, the per-litre price of diesel jumped another 8.82 pesos (about 14 US cents).
"This is a notice that operations may soon become impossible," a group of companies representing bus lines across the country of 116 million said in a statement.
"Fuel prices have reached levels that our operations can no longer afford," it read.
"We are not asking the Government for ayuda," the statement added, using a Filipino term meaning handout.
"We are asking for a fair and sustainable fare that reflects the real cost of operating public transportation."
Millions of Filipinos use buses to get to and from work each day, with prices for a ride ranging from 13 to 15 pesos for the first five kilometres, then jumping about three pesos for each subsequent kilometre.
Contacted by AFP, the transportation department pointed to a Saturday statement saying it "hoped to arrive at a positive decision" on a rate hike in coming days.
The import-dependent Philippines declared a national energy emergency in March and has been forced to cast an ever-wider net for fuel, including purchases of oil from Russia.
Unlike neighbours including Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, fuel prices in the Philippines are unregulated, leaving local transport firms to deal with market fluctuations.
The Marcos administration gave bus operators a one-off subsidy in March of 10,000 pesos for each of their vehicles.
Separate handouts have been given to transport workers including drivers of taxis and the country's ubiquitous jeepneys.
On Tuesday, the energy department said the country had a 57-day reserve of diesel and enough petrol for 56 days.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Companies must rethink global footprints in light of heightened geopolitical risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Geopolitical risks are prompting companies to rethink their global footprints and strengthen localisation in key markets, as businesses seek greater control over supply chains, costs and market access, veteran corporate leader Tan Sri Abdul Wahid Omar said.
Wahid, who is also the non-executive chairman of IOI Corp Bhd, said companies should focus less on the geopolitical event itself and more on how it affects customers, supply chains, cost structures, market access, capital allocation and long-term competitiveness.
"For us in the plantation sector, a geopolitical event may affect our cost of input, fertilisers, energy prices, logistics and trade routes, and our ability to access the market," Wahid said during a panel session at the CGI Global Governance Summit 2026.
He said companies must distinguish between temporary market volatility and structural changes that could affect their competitiveness and future valuations.
Wahid said one example was IOI Corp's downstream operations, including its plants in Germany, which allow the company to serve the European Union market through local production rather than relying entirely on exports from Malaysia.
"When you start to operate on a global scale, yes, there are rewards, but it really comes with risks," he said, adding that companies are increasingly focusing on markets where they could exercise greater control over operations, while maintaining presence in strategically important markets.
Wahid also challenged the view that building resilience against geopolitical shocks necessarily comes at a high cost, saying diversification could instead provide companies with a competitive advantage.
He cited IOI Corp's approach to fertiliser procurement, where having more than one supplier could prevent one from becoming too comfortable and enable the company to secure more competitive pricing and better service.
Similarly, diversifying customers and markets could allow companies to redirect products when a particular market becomes subject to import restrictions or other disruptions.
"So again, my view is actually providing that resilience doesn't necessarily come at cost. In fact, to some areas, it may be to your advantage," he said.
However, Vistra Malaysia country head Celine See said companies should remain mindful that resilience could require additional spending on systems, locations, suppliers, technology and equipment.
She said the challenge was to ensure resilience created value and supported growth rather than simply adding layers of cost and controls.
Companies could respond to a crisis by adding more approval processes, which could slow decision-making when businesses need to react quickly.
"The most resilient organisations are not necessarily the most controlled ones, but they are the organisations that can see things, decide and adapt quickly," she said.
Kiyotaka Sasaki, president of the Core Corporate Governance Research Institute in Japan, said boards should not treat geopolitical developments as external issues that sit outside the company's immediate responsibilities.
"It's not my business. I think that's a mistake. First of all, we need to recognise the issue, then assess the potential impact on our own business," he said.
Sasaki said companies also needed to look beyond compliance with laws and regulations, as geopolitical risks could expose vulnerabilities that were not captured by existing rules or conventional risk frameworks.
Gillian Meller, legal and governance director at MTR Corp in Hong Kong, said boards needed to foster greater "organisational curiosity" by continuously asking what could happen and testing whether existing systems could withstand unexpected disruptions.
"It's really about asking the 'what if' questions," she said, citing scenario exercises that tested how the company would respond if key technology providers or suppliers became unavailable.
Meller said such exercises could expose vulnerabilities before they became crises, allowing companies to identify alternative suppliers, operational arrangements and decision-making processes in advance.

Title: Melaka heads to 16th state election as state assembly dissolved
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: After Johor and Negri Sembilan, Melaka will hold its 16th state election soon following the dissolution of the  state assembly which will take effect tomorrow.
The dissolution of the state assembly was announced by Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh earlier today.
The Melaka state assembly has 28 seats, with the current state government's mandate scheduled to end on Dec 27.
In the 15th Melaka state election held on Nov 20, 2021, Barisan Nasional (BN) formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
However, the state executive council line-up also included PH assemblymen, reflecting the composition of the unity government at the federal level.
On July 16, five Melaka PH assemblymen officially withdrew from the state government after rejecting a proposed amendment to the Melaka State Constitution to create appointed assemblyman positions.
Currently, none of the three coalitions — BN, PH or PN — has officially announced any form of cooperation for the 16th Melaka state election.
BN, however, is expected to cooperate or reach an understanding with PN following a recent statement by Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan, who indicated that political cooperation between BN and PN was almost certain for the Melaka state election.
Rauf, who is also Melaka BN chairman, said yesterday that the coalition would issue official letters to all relevant political parties to present their respective proposals for strategic cooperation.
He had previously stressed that Melaka BN would continue to defend the 21 state assembly seats it won in the previous state election.
At the same time, there has been speculation that PH and Bersatu will form a cooperation for the election.
However, PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the cooperation had yet to be finalised and would depend on the outcome of discussions at the state level.
He also said PH had no problem if BN was not interested in cooperating, but urged the coalition to make its position known so that PH could proceed with preparations for the state election.

Title: Three actors questioned over viral video allegedly mocking Rukun Negara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have recorded statements from three actors involved in a theatre performance to assist investigations into a viral video allegedly mocking the principles of the Rukun Negara.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the three, comprising two women and a man aged between 28 and 47, were detained in Selangor and Johor last Saturday.
He said the performance, which lasted about 10 minutes, was staged at the Penang Performing Arts Centre (PAC) in Penang in 2018.
"There were no police reports lodged when the performance took place in 2018, and the video did not go viral at the time. Therefore, no action was taken. However, the video has now gone viral," he told reporters here today.
Kumar said preliminary investigations found that five actors were involved in the performance, with statements recorded from three of them.
"One of the other two actors has been confirmed dead, while the other is believed to be in the United Kingdom (UK), based on Immigration Department records," he said.
He said the theatre director, a UK national, had also been confirmed to have left Malaysia and returned to his home country.
Kumar said the three detained individuals were released on police bail after their statements were recorded.
Forensic examinations of their devices and social media accounts also found no recordings of the performance, he said.
He said police were tracing the Internet Protocol (IP) address to identify the person responsible for uploading the video.
Kumar added that the case was being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and would be referred to the Attorney General's Chambers for further instructions.
Last Saturday, media reported that the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) was investigating a video of a stage performance allegedly insulting the institution of the Malay Rulers and the Rukun Negara.

Title: MCMC not decision-maker in  Na'im Brundage TikTok accounts blocking, High Court rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today allowed a preliminary objection by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and four others against Bersatu Youth leader Na'im Brundage's application for leave to initiate judicial review over the blocking of his two TikTok accounts.
Judge Norliza Othman, in allowing the objection, said the leave application was premised on the assumption that MCMC (3rd respondent) had directed TikTok to block Na'im's accounts, which could not form the basis for judicial review.
She said although the threshold for leave to initiate judicial review was low, an application should be dismissed if the applicant could not establish an arguable case at the substantive stage.
"In this case, the very first hurdle that the applicant needs to overcome is identifying who decided to censor and block the TikTok account. It is definitely not the third respondent. The third respondent merely carried out its legal administrative action, which does not amount to a decision.
"That does not constitute a decision that can form the basis of the duty usually relied upon for an application under Order 53 of the Rules of Court," she said.
The court also ordered Na'im to pay RM5,000 in costs to the first to third respondents and RM5,000 to the fourth and fifth respondents.
Na'im filed the judicial review application on June 24, 2024, naming MCMC chief network security officer Datuk Dr Mohamed Sulaiman Sultan Suhaibuddeen, the MCMC chairman, MCMC, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and the Government of Malaysia as respondents.
Na'im was represented by lawyer Latheefa Koya, while lawyer A. Ruebankumar appeared for the first to third respondents and Senior Federal Counsel Ainna Sherina Saipolamin represented the minister and the government.
Speaking to reporters after the ruling, Latheefa said her client would appeal the decision.
Na'im had sought a certiorari order to quash the respondents' decision, as stated in a letter dated April 1, 2024, to block his two TikTok accounts.
He alleged that the blocking of the accounts contravened Section 3(3) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, claiming that the legislation contained no provision authorising such action.
Na'im alleged that the decision was "invalid, unlawful, irrational, procedurally improper, unjust and a violation of fundamental justice".
In his supporting affidavit, he said he frequently uploaded videos to his two TikTok accounts expressing his views on current issues of public interest, including social, political and economic matters.
He said he discovered in March 2024 that both accounts had been blocked and were no longer accessible. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: S'gor Bersatu Youth chief fails to initiate judicial review against MCMC, Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor Bersatu Youth chief Na'im Brundage has failed in his bid for leave to initiate a judicial review over the blocking of two of his TikTok accounts three years ago.
The High Court here ruled in favour of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil in their preliminary objection to Na'im's application.
Judge Norliza Othman found that the decision to block the accounts had been taken by TikTok and not by MCMC.
Besides MCMC and Fahmi, those named in the preliminary objection also included MCMC Network Security chief officer Datuk Dr Mohamed Sulaiman Sultan Suhaibuddeen, the MCMC chairman and the government.
In today's proceedings, the five parties were named as the first to fifth applicants, while Na'im, who is also Bersatu Youth communications and new media department director, was named as the respondent.
In her judgment, Norliza said MCMC had made no decision that could be subject to judicial review, as the action to block or suspend the accounts was taken by TikTok.
"MCMC only took administrative action by informing TikTok about compliance issues involving the platform's guidelines, while the subsequent action was TikTok's decision.
"A judicial review under Order 53 of the Rules of Court 2012 concerns the decision-making process and is not an appeal against the merits of a decision," she said.
Norliza said the key question that needed to be determined was which party had made the decision to block the respondent's TikTok accounts.
"The court referred to the letter dated Oct 24, 2024, and the respondent's lawyer was informed that MCMC had certain duties and powers to issue warnings to TikTok regarding the publication of the content," she said.
She added that it was after the letter was sent that TikTok made the decision to block Na'im's accounts.
"Based on this, the action to block or suspend the account was not taken by MCMC. It is clear from the statement itself that the decision to block or suspend the TikTok account did not come from MCMC.
"They only took administrative action by issuing a warning to TikTok regarding the failure to comply with guidelines, before TikTok took action to block or suspend Na'im's account," she said.
She said the court can only review the manner in which a decision was made, rather than determining whether the decision itself was reasonable or justified on its merits.
"The respondent's application (for judicial review) is based on the assumption that MCMC instructed TikTok to block or censor his account, whereas that decision was made by TikTok.
"MCMC only carried out legal and administrative actions. It cannot be considered a decision that is subject to judicial review," she said.
Na'im had discovered that two of his TikTok accounts were blocked in 2023, after which he filed an application for judicial review on June 24, 2024.
Na'im had sought a certiorari order to quash the decision to block both accounts.
In his supporting affidavit, he said the two social media accounts served as a platform for him to express his views and opinions on current issues.

Title: Court of Appeal sets Jan 7 next year to deliver decision on Malaysian Bar's Najib pardon appeal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA:  The Court of Appeal has set Jan 7 next year to deliver its decision on the appeal by the Malaysian Bar who is seeking leave to commence a judicial review to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board's (FTPB) decision to reduce former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's prison sentence and fine in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case.
Lawyer Zainur Zakaria, representing the Malaysian Bar, confirmed the date when contacted by Bernama today.
On July 31, the Court of Appeal three-man bench comprising Datuk Lim Chong Fong, Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli and Datuk Leonard David Shim heard the appeal and reserved its decision.
The Malaysian Bar is appealing the Nov 2024 High Court's dismissal of its application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings to quash the Pardons Board's decision.
In the application filed in April 2024 against the Pardons Board of the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya, and Najib, the Bar had sought a declaration that the Pardons Board's decision on Jan 29, 2024, reducing Najib's prison sentence from 12 years to six years, resulting in his early release on Aug 23, 2028, is illegal, unconstitutional and void.
It is also seeking a declaration that the Pardons Board's decision to reduce Najib's fine from RM210 million to RM50 million is similarly illegal, unconstitutional and void.
Najib, 73, has been serving his sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, after being convicted of misappropriating RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd.
He filed a petition for a royal pardon on Sept 2, 2022, which resulted in the Pardons Board halving his prison sentence and reducing his fine from RM210 million to RM50 million.
On Sept 18 this year, Najib was granted a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, subject to his payment of the RM50 million fine.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar was reported as saying that Najib has
yet to pay the fine
stipulated as a condition for serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teens as young as 13 caught producing, selling animated CSAM - Cops
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Some of the eight minors detained in a nationwide operation targeting child sexual abuse material (CSAM) were found to have produced and sold animated child sexual abuse material online.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar said the material was sold to online communities with similar interests, with some pieces reportedly priced at between RM50 and RM60.
"The eight children aged between 13 and 18, comprising seven boys and a girl, were detained. Besides downloading the material, some also produced their own animations and sold them.
"The buyers were from communities with an inclination towards such material," he said.
Kumar said the communities were formed online, with members not necessarily knowing one another personally.
"Those who have accessed such material will find groups with similar interests and inclinations, forming small online communities.
"They do not know one another. This is happening online, including through Telegram. What is worrying is not so much the price, but the trend and where it is heading. This is what we need to take seriously," he said.
On how children learned to produce such material, Kumar said it could be learned through various means, including online platforms, social media and artificial intelligence (AI) technology.
However, he said investigations were ongoing to determine whether they had been exposed to such material by individuals or other parties.
The youngest was a 13-year-old girl, but police were still investigating the amount of CSAM linked to her and the purpose for which the material was possessed.
Kumar said the parents of the children only became aware of their activities after the arrests, while investigations were ongoing to determine how they were first exposed to such material.
He said transactions for the sale of the material could be carried out through various methods, including e-wallets, PayPal and Touch'n Go.
"Our children are far more proficient than adults when it comes to social media use. That is a fact. Therefore, continuous monitoring is necessary, and this must begin at home," he said.
On action against the eight children, Kumar said investigations would be completed before the cases were referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) for further instructions and advice.
"Police also has counsellors to assist children facing such cases, but efforts to raise awareness must be carried out continuously and should not stop after enforcement action," he said.
Earlier, 53 individuals aged between 13 and 56 were detained in Op Pedo Bersepadu PDRM-MCMC 3.0, conducted nationwide from Sept 14 to 16.
Of the total, 52 were Malaysians and one was a Bangladeshi, while eight of those arrested were children.

Title: Thai national among two arrested for misappropriating petrol
Article:
KANGAR: The Perlis branch of the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has arrested two people for allegedly misappropriating about 300 litres of petrol in a raid on an unnumbered house in Kampung Titi Tinggi Ulu, Padang Besar, last night.
Its director Rohaida Hassan said the woman in her 40s and the Thai man in his 30s were arrested during the raid at about 8pm by eight enforcement officers following a week-long intelligence operation.
"During the raid, we found that petrol was being transferred from a locally registered Proton Waja into a Toyota Hilux bearing a Thai registration number," she said in a statement today.
She said further inspection of the Proton Waja found that its rear fuel tank had been modified, while the Toyota Hilux was also found to have a modified fuel tank underneath the vehicle.
Rohaida said enforcement action was taken under Section 21 of the Control of Supplies Act 1961.
"About 300 litres of petrol, worth RM597, were seized, while the total value of the seized items is estimated at RM98,097," she said.

Title: Seven religious school students arrested over two bullying cases in Rompin
Article:
KUANTAN: Police have arrested seven religious school students in Rompin over their alleged involvement in two separate bullying incidents this month.
The victims were three 14-year-old students studying and residing at the school hostel.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the first incident, on Sept 12, involved two victims, with police arresting five suspects comprising Form Four and Form Five students aged 16 and 17.
"The second incident also involved a Form Two student, and six students were picked up from the school for investigations. Four of the suspects were also involved in the first incident, and all have been released on police bail.
"We are finalising the investigation papers, including the performance and disciplinary reports of the victims and suspects, which will be provided by the school. We hope to complete all the paperwork today," he told reporters at the state police headquarters here today.
Earlier, Azry witnessed the handover-of-duty ceremony for the head of the Pahang police Management Department between outgoing Senior Assistant Commissioner Mohd Fakhrurazie Che Sulaiman and Superintendent Afandi Hussin.
Fakhrurazie will head the Anti-Money Laundering Crime Investigation Unit under the Inspector-General of Police Secretariat at Bukit Aman.
Meanwhile, Azry said officers from the Rompin district police headquarters went to the school after the incident was reported on Sept 17.
"We take the matter seriously and held discussions with the school management. We want to prevent any similar incidents from occurring on the premises," he said when asked whether the school was attempting to cover up the incident.
Both cases were investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting, which carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
It was
reported on Sept 19
that two religious school students were assaulted by five senior students after one of them allegedly skipped a religious class while the other was allegedly accused of conspiring with him. The victims suffered injuries to their arms and bodies.
The incident came to light after the mother of one of the victims,
Siti Rohani Yusof
, claimed that her family had been left traumatised after the suspects allegedly hit her son with a broomstick and threatened him with a penknife.

Title: Rauf vows Melaka public services to continue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The dissolution of the Melaka assembly will not disrupt the administration or essential public services, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said.
He said the government would continue to carry out its duties as a caretaker government until a new administration is formed after the election.
"I wish to assure the people of Melaka that the dissolution of the assembly does not mean government affairs will come to a halt.
"The administration, public services, welfare of the people, security and daily government operations will continue as usual.
"Our priority during this period is to ensure the administration remains orderly, public services are not disrupted and the interests of the people are protected," he told a press conference at Seri Negeri.
Rauf said all government departments and agencies, as well as local authorities, would continue to carry out their duties in accordance with existing laws, regulations and directives.
Earlier, Rauf announced that the Melaka assembly would be
dissolved
tomorrow.
He said Yang di-Pertua Negeri Melaka Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam had consented to the dissolution following an audience earlier today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More than 2.1 million CSAM, porn files uncovered since 2024
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 2.1 million files containing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and pornography have been uncovered through Op Pedo and Operation Cyber Guardian since 2024.
The number of arrests under Op Pedo has also increased significantly over the past three years.
Federal Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M Kumar said the two operations had resulted in 170 arrests and the seizure of 369 items of evidence, in addition to the discovery of 2,123,887 CSAM and pornography files.
He said the police and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) integrated Op Pedo 1.0 in 2024 resulted in 13 arrests, before the figure rose to 31 under Op Pedo 2.0 last year.
"In Op Pedo 3.0, carried out from Sept 14 to 16, the number of arrests increased to 53 individuals.
"Each time an operation is conducted, the figures become bigger and continue to increase.
"Therefore, we need more aggressive integrated action, not only from the punitive aspect but also in terms of awareness," he said in a press conference at Bukit Aman today.
A comparison of the three Op Pedo operations also showed an increase in the number of investigation papers, from 13 in 2024 to 29 last year and 52 this year.
The number of items seized also increased from 37 in Op Pedo 1.0 to 82 in Op Pedo 2.0 and 95 in the latest operation.
Op Pedo 1.0, conducted on Dec 23, 2024, involved six states, before its coverage was expanded to all 14 police contingents through Op Pedo 2.0 and 3.0.
Cumulatively, the three Op Pedo operations resulted in 97 arrests, 94 investigation papers and the seizure of 214 items of evidence.
A total of 1,573,193 CSAM and pornography files were also discovered through the three operations, comprising 40,000 files in Op Pedo 1.0, 880,000 in Op Pedo 2.0 and 653,193 in Op Pedo 3.0.
Apart from Op Pedo, police also conducted Operation Cyber Guardian, with the first operation on March 20, 2025, resulting in four arrests, the seizure of 29 items of evidence and the discovery of 52,000 files.
Operation Cyber Guardian II, conducted from April 6 to 8 this year, resulted in 69 arrests, the seizure of 126 items of evidence and the discovery of 498,694 files.
In a related development, MCMC recorded 12,529 applications involving pornographic and CSAM content on social media and internet messaging services between Jan 1 and Sept 21 this year.
Of the total, 11,665 pieces of content were taken down, while 1,031 websites were shut down by MCMC during the same period.
Kumar said the rising figures called for a continuous approach that was not solely focused on enforcement.
He said police and MCMC each had a special team to monitor CSAM and pornographic content, but efforts to curb such activities required the involvement of other agencies, non-governmental organisations (NGOs), parents and the community.
"Although we are working tirelessly to monitor and take action, success will not be achieved without the involvement of other agencies.
"Punitive action is very important, but moral awareness is more important, and this needs to be carried out continuously," he said.
He said parental supervision on children's use of social media also needed to be increased, given young people's skills in using technology and digital platforms.
Also present was MCMC chief network security officer Datuk Dr Mohamed Sulaiman Sultan Suhaibuddeen.

Title: Migrants turn to sea routes to sneak into Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: Illegal migrants entering Kelantan are now more frequently using sea routes from Tak Bai, Thailand, rather than the Sungai Golok border, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said.
He said the shift had not affected security controls along the land border, which remain jointly enforced by the General Operations Force, armed forces and other relevant agencies.
"So far, when we arrest migrants, they are not coming through the Thai border there, but entering by sea. Many are coming through routes from Tak Bai and using the Kelantan River.
"Police are now increasing surveillance of these sea routes, while working with the Thai authorities to curb the activities of groups believed to be involved in bringing migrants into the country," he told reporters after the September 2026 Monthly Assembly at the Kelantan police headquarters today.
Yusoff said police had also shared information with the Thai authorities on groups identified as being active in the Tak Bai area for further action.
He said surveillance was also being conducted at certain areas that previously had access through riverbanks, including locations without jetty structures but where existing routes were being used.
Meanwhile, Yusoff said 96 illegal jetties had been demolished to strengthen border controls, while action would be taken against any newly built structures found to compromise security.
On another matter, he advised members of the public not to take matters into their own hands against Myanmar refugees or migrants suspected of committing offences, but instead to channel information to the authorities.
He said taking such action could trigger fights or other untoward incidents, while also complicating enforcement efforts.
"We are still capable of dealing with any crime as well as this border issue. So report it to us and let the authorities take action," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OGX Group ventures into renewable energy, targets data centre market
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: OGX Group Bhd has ventured into the renewable energy (RE) industry, targeting opportunities in Malaysia's growing data centre market through battery energy storage systems (BESS).
In a statement today, the information technology infrastructure solutions provider said its wholly owned subsidiary OGX Green Tech Sdn Bhd will spearhead the new business.
The group said Zhejiang Hyxi Technology Co Ltd (Hyxi), a China-based energy storage and inverter specialist with a presence across Europe, has appointed OGX Green Tech as an authorised distributor to market, distribute and sell Hyxi's products in Malaysia.
"The new business segment will focus on the distribution of BESS, inverters and batteries, serving both residential and commercial and industrial (C&I) customers in Malaysia.
"In addition, OGX Green Tech also intends to tap into the growing demand for energy storage solutions within Malaysia's rapidly expanding data centre industry, where data centre operators are increasingly seeking cleaner and more resilient alternatives to conventional diesel backup generators to support the surge in artificial intelligence, cloud computing and data-intensive workloads," it said.
OGX executive director and managing director Tan Suan Loong said the group's brand-centric model has driven its business, with the RE expansion a natural progression of this strategy.
"The appointment by Hyxi brings together its technology and product expertise in energy storage solutions with OGX's local market access, distribution capabilities and systems integration experience.
"This combination provides us with a strong platform to establish and scale our presence in the energy storage segment as a new and complementary growth vertical for OGX," he said.
Tan said the transition towards cleaner and more resilient energy solutions is creating growing opportunities across the residential, C&I and data centre segments.
"Through OGX Green Tech and our appointment by Hyxi, we are well positioned to address this demand by combining proven energy storage solutions with OGX's existing customer relationships, market reach and systems integration capabilities.
"We believe this new business can broaden our revenue base and position OGX to participate in the long-term growth of Malaysia's energy transition," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan residents prepare for Super El Nino, fear wells could run dry
Article:
KOTA BARU: Residents relying on underground water have begun making early preparations for the Super El Nino phenomenon, which is expected to affect the state from November.
Most said they were worried that their underground wells, typically 20 to 40 feet deep, could dry up during prolonged hot weather.
Grocery shopkeeper Abdul Aziz Wahab, 40, said residents were looking for ways to prevent water shortages.
"We are worried that we may face water shortages if the Super El Nino hits, so we are making early preparations," said the father of five who is from Kota Baru.
Housewife Nor Fatihah Salleh, 37, said residents relying on underground water were concerned about having an adequate supply during the dry spell.
"I have been using underground water for five years and after hearing the prediction about the coming phenomenon, I plan to dig the well deeper," said the mother of two from Pendek.
Meanwhile, Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department director Farhan Sufyan Borhan said the department was ready to face the expected Super El Nino from November, particularly the increased risk of open burning.
He said the state was expected to experience hotter conditions towards early next year, especially during the transition between the northeast and southwest monsoons.
"Based on information from the Malaysian Meteorological Department, the Super El Nino is expected to begin in November and continue into early 2027.
"While Kelantan may still receive rain during the northeast monsoon, the early part of next year could bring hotter and drier conditions," he said.
Farhan said temperatures could reach about 38 to 39 degrees Celsius in Kelantan, although some areas in Perlis could record temperatures as high as 41 degrees Celsius.
He said the department was particularly concerned about a sharp increase in open-burning cases if preventive measures and public awareness were lacking.
"Open burning could increase significantly, especially during the dry period. This could make firefighting operations more challenging if water levels drop," he said.
On another note, Farhan said the department had recorded 1,904 calls involving open burning so far this year, compared with 375 calls throughout last year.
He said the department had 33 fire engines, 10 water tankers, 633 personnel and 220 volunteer firefighters stationed at 22 fire stations statewide.
"Although open-burning cases are high this year, water levels remain normal. If water levels fall next year, obtaining water from rivers, ponds and lakes for firefighting could become more difficult," he said.
Farhan said peatland areas in Bachok, Pasir Mas, Pasir Puteh and Tanah Merah were among the areas of concern, as fires there could take longer to extinguish.
He said most open-burning incidents were caused by people deliberately burning rubbish or clearing land, which was considered a cheap and effective way to prepare land but could become dangerous if not controlled.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor man says he collected recyclables to sell, not trouble neighbours
Article:
JOHOR BARU: "I was collecting the items to sell, not to trouble my neighbours," said a physically disabled elderly man after authorities cleared about 13 tonnes of recyclable materials from his home in Taman Permas Jaya.
A photo showed rubbish and recyclable materials piled along the front gate, covering much of the pavement and spilling towards the roadside.
The man, in his 60s, stored recyclable items inside and outside his house, to the dismay of neighbours who complained of foul odours, pests and an unsightly mess.
He said the items were for sale but admitted he had not expected authorities to take action against him.
"I collect the items to sell. I do not want to trouble my neighbours.
"I was going to sell them tomorrow or the day after. I will not do this again. This is the last time," he said.
Meanwhile, a neighbour, who identified himself only as Tharanya, in his 60s, said residents were relieved by the cleanup.
He said about three lorries were used to haul away the materials from the house.
"We are relieved because there had been no solution to this problem. I had repeatedly told him to stop, but he continued," he said.
Tharanya said residents hoped the man would not resume the activity and that the authorities would continue to monitor the house.
He added that the man's van and car had also been used to store recyclable materials.
State SWCorp removed the recyclable materials and issued a notice to the owner.
He may face a fine of RM10,000 to RM100,000, up to five years' jail, or both under Section 71(1) of Act 672.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tasik Bera enforcement: Five arrested, investigation papers to be referred to DPP
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 22 — Police have received 24 reports in connection with operations at the Tasik Bera Conservation Forest Reserve in Bera as of yesterday.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the reports were lodged by members of the Orang Asli community and enforcement personnel.
“The operation is ongoing, and we urge the public to cooperate with enforcement personnel in carrying out their duties,” he told reporters after attending the handover-of-duties ceremony for the Pahang Police Management Department chief at the Pahang Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
Azry Akmar said the investigation papers on five individuals arrested on Sept 15 for allegedly obstructing enforcement officers during the operation would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor soon.
Police had earlier arrested four women and a man, aged between their 30s and 60s, to assist in investigations under Section 186 of the Penal Code.
In an unrelated development, Azry Akmar said police had opened two investigation papers following a recent altercation at a religious school in Bukit Ibam, Rompin.
He said the first case involved two male victims, both aged 14, and five suspects who were Form Four and Form Five students.
“The second case involved another 14-year-old male victim and six suspects. Further investigations found that four of the suspects were also involved in the first case,” he said, adding that the investigation was being conducted under Section 147 of the Penal Code.
Azry Akmar said both investigation papers would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor today for further instructions.
At the event, Azry Akmar witnessed the handover of duties between outgoing Pahang Police Management Department chief SAC Mohd Fakhrurazie Che Sulaiman and his successor, Supt Afandi Hussin.
Mohd Fakhrurazie has been transferred to Bukit Aman to head the Anti-Money Laundering Crime Investigation Unit under the Inspector-General of Police Secretariat.  — Bernama

Title: PKR’s Hassan Karim urges Anwar to retain Anthony Loke ahead of major transport projects
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Sept 22 — Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim has called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to persuade Anthony Loke to remain as transport minister to ensure the completion of several key infrastructure projects, including those in Johor.
The PKR lawmaker expressed concern that Loke’s resignation could jeopardise ongoing projects, including those in Johor.
“These include projects such as the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS), the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), the proposed Pasir Gudang railway line, and the rapid transit system, which have yet to be fully implemented.
“However, Anwar should first hear out Loke’s reasons before deciding to accept his offer to resign.
“I hope the prime minister takes my view into consideration and persuades Loke to stay. We are drawing closer to the general election and Loke is an asset to the government and the ruling Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition,” he told reporters after a dialogue session between transport operators and businesspeople, with officials from the Johor chapter of the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) and the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) at Lepak Corner here today.
Hassan said his remarks were based on precedents where national leaders had been known to reject the resignation of members of their administration, including during the federal government of the first prime minister, Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj.
“This demonstrates that a resignation need not necessarily be accepted, particularly when the services of a minister or administration member are still deemed essential,” he said, citing the recent example of Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh rejecting the resignation of Datuk Muhamad Akmal Saleh as a state executive councillor.
On a personal level, Hassan described Loke’s decision to offer his resignation following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak as a responsible move.
However, the social activist noted that the final decision on whether Loke should leave the Cabinet rests with the prime minister.
“Anwar gave his assurance and has indicated he would listen to the outgoing transport minister’s reasons before deciding,” he said.

Title: Melaka heads for polls as CM Rauf Yusoh confirms assembly set for dissolution tomorrow
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 22 — The Melaka State Legislative Assembly will be dissolved tomorrow to pave the way for the 16th state election.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the matter at a press conference at the Seri Negeri Complex here today.
He said the dissolution had received the consent of Melaka Governor Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
“I would like to take this opportunity to express my deepest appreciation to the Governor of Melaka for his consent and wisdom in carrying out his functions as provided for under the law,” he said.
Ab Rauf said State Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum had also submitted the notice of dissolution to the Election Commission (EC).
The last Melaka state election was held on Nov 20, 2021, after four assemblymen withdrew their support for then Chief Minister Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali, causing the state government to collapse.
They were former Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Idris Haron (BN-Sungai Udang), Datuk Nor Azman Hassan (BN-Pantai Kundor), Datuk Noor Effandi Ahmad (Bersatu-Telok Mas) and independent Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee (Pengkalan Batu).
Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats in the election, securing a more than two-thirds majority to form the state government.
Of the 21 seats, Umno won 18, MCA two and MIC one.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five seats, four of which through DAP and one through Amanah, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two.
The composition of the assembly subsequently changed after Rembia assemblyman Datuk Muhammad Jailani Khamis left BN for PAS, while Bemban assemblyman Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub was expelled from Bersatu and became an independent while remaining in the opposition bloc.
The changes reduced BN’s representation to 20 seats, but it retained a comfortable majority in the 28-seat assembly and continued to govern the state.
The current assembly’s term had been due to expire on Dec 27. — Bernama

Title: Three actors out on bail as police hunt uploader of viral Rukun Negara clip from 2018
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Bukit Aman have released three local actors on police bail after questioning them over a viral video of a 2018 theatre performance allegedly mocking the Rukun Negara, while investigators hunt for the person who re-uploaded the footage.
Federal Criminal Investigation Department irector Datuk M. Kumar said the performers, a man and two women aged 28, 29 and 47 respectively, were picked up in Selangor and Johor last Saturday.
“The three have since been released on police bail after their statements were recorded, and checks found no content from the performance on their mobile phones or other devices.
“We recorded their statements and released them on police bail because they cooperated and we had completed checks on their devices. Nothing was found, so there was no justification to remand them,” he told a press conference at the federal police headquarters here.
Kumar said police had identified five actors featured in the clip, adding that one has since diedf and the other is believed to currently be in the United Kingdom based on immigration records.
He said investigators are now tracing the person who uploaded the eight-year-old footage online, including through relevant Internet Protocol addresses.
“Someone has now circulated what happened in 2018 and we are tracking down the person who uploaded the video,” he said.
The performance was staged behind closed doors at a performing arts centre in Penang in 2018 as part of a competition involving several groups.
The performing arts centre has since closed, Kumar said.
He added that investigations showed the performance director is a UK national who has since left Malaysia.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. — Bernama

Title: Melaka heads for polls? CM Ab Rauf set to make big announcement today
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 22 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to announce the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly at 2pm today, paving the way for the 16th state election.
The announcement is expected to be made at Kompleks Seri Negeri in Ayer Keroh.
Speculation over an imminent dissolution intensified after the state executive council meeting, usually held on Wednesdays, was brought forward by a day.
Ab Rauf is understood to have chaired the meeting at noon today.
The Chief Minister’s Office has also invited members of the media to a press conference scheduled for 2pm.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats contested, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
The current state assembly’s term is due to expire on Dec 27. — Bernama

Title: No drug arrests for a week? Kelantan police chief says two station heads get reprimand letters
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — Two police station chiefs (OCSs) in Kelantan have received reprimand letters after they failed to record any drug-related arrests for a week, said state police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat.
He said further action might be taken if the OCSs did not improve their performance.
He said the state police headquarters is monitoring seven police stations with regard to enforcement against drug abuse and trafficking.
“If a particular station has no arrests at all for a week, I will ensure that a team from the Contingent Police Headquarters goes to the area.
“If the special task force from the IPK manages to make an arrest, the OCS concerned will be reprimanded,” he told a press conference after the Kelantan contingent police monthly assembly here today.
Mohd Yusoff said the performance of each police station is monitored weekly and presented at meetings with the head of the Narcotics Department.
He said OCSs who receive reprimand letters must ensure that their performance meets the key performance indicators again the following week.
