Mohd Yusoff said a post-mortem would be conducted on Oct 15 following a three-month pilot period to identify the reasons certain police stations failed to meet the stipulated KPIs. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: OCS is short for Officer-in-Charge of Station.

Title: Malaysia’s research has potential, now it needs to leave the lab, says higher education minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia’s research and innovation ecosystem has recorded more than 500 matched patents valued at over RM2 billion through the Malaysian R&D Commercialisation Portal, involving more than 120 active missions, showing that the country does not lack ideas or talent.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the milestone demonstrated Malaysia’s immense capacity for innovation, provided the gap between academic research and commercial market demands could be bridged effectively.
“Malaysia had many good researchers, ideas and promising innovations, but too many of them remained at the university level.
“For the first time, we are creating a dedicated platform for university researchers to bring their ideas directly to industry, investors and potential partners,” he said during the opening ceremony of the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.
Meanwhile, Zambry urged local industry players to look inside Malaysian universities for technological solutions before turning to foreign providers.
He said while local institutions possess extensive talent, facilities and intellectual property, a lack of confidence often leads businesses to seek solutions outside the country.
“Research cannot end with a publication. Innovation cannot end with a patent. A prototype cannot remain in the laboratory. A discovery must become a solution. A prototype must become a product. And an idea must become an opportunity,” he said.
Zambry also called on investors to view university researchers not only as academics, but also as innovators, entrepreneurs and potential business partners.
Over the three-day summit, URIIS 2026 will cover at least nine strategic sectors, including food security, healthcare, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, green technology, mobility, defence and biodiversity. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Neither MB Ismail Lasim nor I was summoned by Negeri Sembilan Ruler for an audience
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said neither he nor Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was summoned for an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Negeri Sembilan here yesterday.
“No. Neither the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar nor I was ever summoned for an audience. We only learnt about it through the media,” he said when asked at a press conference after officiating the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026 here today.
He said the ongoing dispute in Negeri Sembilan should be resolved properly, with due regard for both legal interpretations and the state’s institutions.
“In my view, this is not merely a question of legal interpretation and powers. The institutions and establishment in Negeri Sembilan must also be respected,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Negeri Sembilan in the capital yesterday, with the meeting lasting nearly an hour.
The audience followed Tuanku Muhriz’s decision to revoke the appointments of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council members with immediate effect, after finding that they had breached their oaths of office.
Ismail, however, has disputed the validity of the move, arguing that the dismissal or termination of an executive councillor without the advice or request of the Menteri Besar was legally flawed, unconstitutional and had no legal effect. — Bernama

Title: Finance pros cannot escape geopolitics in a changing world, says deputy finance minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Finance professionals must adapt to a rapidly changing global landscape shaped by geopolitical shifts, climate and sustainability challenges, artificial intelligence (AI) and growing concerns over trust.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the transformation of the global environment in recent years had created new challenges for businesses and finance professionals, requiring them to rethink how financial systems and structures are designed.
“If you are the ‘architect’ of a financial structure, you cannot run away from geopolitics. This is the time for accountants to equip themselves with geopolitical and geoeconomics knowledge to deal with the challenges to come,” he said in his keynote address at the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants Leadership Exchange Forum 2026.
Liew said the years ahead would be different from the period preceding 2020, with the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent geopolitical conflicts transforming the global landscape.
As such, he emphasised the need for financial professionals to understand geopolitical developments worldwide, particularly as businesses face growing risks to investment, technology and supply chains.
He said supply chain resilience was one of the key issues, noting that for a long time, businesses had assumed goods would move automatically by container ships without having to consider their sources or the need for alternative sources of raw materials and what to do in the event of supply chain disruptions.
“I think these are the questions that those in the financial systems will have to ask,” said Liew.
On climate and sustainability, he said these are issues that accountants can no longer avoid, adding that the profession needs to consider ways to measure and manage them.
At the same time, he noted that accountants and businesses would need to adapt and transform their practices to maximise the benefits that AI has to offer.
The Leadership Exchange Forum, themed “Finance as Architect: Aligning Policy, Practice and Technology in the Age of AI”, brings together policymakers, finance leaders, technology experts and industry practitioners to examine how AI and data are reshaping the finance function and its role in driving business growth.
The forum will examine how finance professionals can bridge the gap between technology and human expertise while maintaining professional judgement, ethics and trust. — Bernama

Title: From ‘Made in Malaysia’ to ‘Made by Malaysia’: Govt wants R&D to turn more research into commercial gains
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The government is looking to strengthen Malaysia’s research and development (R&D) ecosystem through more market-driven funding mechanisms and closer industry collaboration, said Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said Malaysia is shifting from a “Made in Malaysia” to a “Made by Malaysia” approach as it seeks to strengthen value creation and drive economic upgrading, with R&D playing a central role.
While Malaysia’s R&D spending has reached about one per cent of gross domestic product, or nearly RM20 billion, he said the main challenge is turning research into commercial results.
“The issue is not just the amount of R&D, but whether it leads to value capture in the country, including ownership of intellectual property and the ability of local firms to compete globally.
“What we (government) want to do is actually to make sure that we provide a capital market that can help support the development of local firms along the way by providing capital,” he said during a panel session at the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026.
Amir Hamzah said the government is focusing on aligning research efforts with national priorities, including the New Industrial Master Plan, the National Semiconductor Strategy and the Energy Transition Roadmap, to attract investments and improve commercialisation prospects.
He said capital is already available through initiatives such as the GEAR-uP programme, under which government-linked investment companies have committed RM120 billion over five years, alongside about RM10 billion channelled into venture and growth funds such as Dana Perintis, Dana Permaju and Dana Impak.
However, he said the gap lies in the ability of researchers and institutions to bring innovations to the market.
“Sometimes the product may be brilliant, but if you do not know how to position and sell it, investors will not come in,” he said.
Amir Hamzah said universities also have a critical role to play by shifting towards more applied research and strengthening partnerships with industry, while continuing to build foundational knowledge through fundamental research. — Bernama

Title: Piranha in Pahang? Fisheries Department calls in Aquaria KLCC for DNA backup
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — The Department of Fisheries Malaysia (DOF) will collaborate with Aquaria KLCC to identify fish suspected to be piranhas at Klau Dam, Raub, Pahang, using DNA or environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis.
Director-General of Fisheries Datuk Adnan Hussain said the collaboration would leverage live piranha specimens and existing DNA data held by Aquaria KLCC to determine the fish’s identity.
“We cannot confirm whether it is a piranha or pacu because we do not have a physical specimen. I hope this collaboration with Aquaria KLCC will help resolve the matter, including identifying the fish at the genus and species levels,” he told reporters after officiating the Teluk Bahang Marine Education Centre here today.
He said preliminary analysis by the Glami Lemi Fisheries Research Institute (FRI), based on video footage obtained, indicated that the fish’s morphological characteristics more closely resembled those of a piranha. However, definitive identification was not possible without a physical specimen.
Adnan said the Pahang Fisheries Department had instructed inland fishermen at Klau Dam to retain and surrender any fish resembling piranhas for examination of their morphology, scales and teeth.
He said there had been reports from fishermen of similar fish being found, but the specimens had already been discarded.
“Currently, we do not have concrete evidence of a population of this species at Klau Dam. There have also been no reports of unusual mortality among local fish species or attacks involving anglers or members of the public,” he said.
He said if the fish was confirmed to be a piranha, a species native to the Amazon basin, it could theoretically adapt and reproduce in Malaysia’s ecosystem due to the similarity in equatorial climates.
A video of a fish allegedly resembling a piranha being caught by an inland fisherman at Klau Dam recently sparked concern among netizens over the possible presence of the non-native species.
The Pahang Fisheries Department’s investigation found that the fish had been caught using a cast net by a local resident on Aug 26, before the video was circulated through a WhatsApp group.
Meanwhile, Adnan said DOF would meet with online platform operators following allegations that prohibited fish species were still being sold on their platforms.
He said possession of prohibited fish species requires special approval from the DOF, while imported live fish, including permitted species, must be accompanied by a health certificate to ensure they are free from diseases that could threaten the local ecosystem.
He added that the DOF would continue conducting inspections at ornamental fish premises nationwide to ensure compliance with regulations governing the possession and keeping of prohibited fish species. — Bernama

Title: After retiring as police No 2, Ayob Khan takes on new role as UTeM board chairman
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 22 — Former Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay has been appointed chairman of the Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) Board of Directors for a three-year term effective Sept 16.
In a statement here today, UTeM said the appointment, approved by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir, succeeds Datuk Husaini Omar, whose term has ended.
The university said Ayob Khan’s extensive experience in leadership and senior management in one of the country’s key departments was expected to strengthen the UTeM Board’s role in steering the university’s strategic direction sustainably.
“UTeM believes his extensive experience and strong strategic management credentials will enable him to lead the UTeM Board in addressing the challenges ahead,” it said.
The university said his appointment was expected to bring a new dimension to UTeM’s strategic leadership, particularly in strengthening governance, strategic networks and the university’s role in developing technical education in the country.
UTeM also expressed its highest appreciation and gratitude to Husaini for his contributions, commitment and service during his tenure as chairman of the UTeM Board of Directors. — Bernama

Title: As parents age, Malaysia must plan for neurodivergent adults too, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Planning for neurodivergent individuals must extend beyond childhood intervention to cover their needs throughout their lifespan, particularly as their parents and caregivers grow older.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said this was increasingly important as neurodivergent individuals were living longer and Malaysia was rapidly transitioning towards an ageing society, with those aged 60 and above expected to make up 15 per cent of the population by 2036.
“Today, we are confronting two realities at the same time. Firstly, as healthcare and living conditions improve, neurodivergent individuals are living longer, fuller lives and secondly, Malaysia is rapidly transitioning towards an aged nation status, with citizens aged 60 and above expected to reach 15 per cent of our population by 2036,” she said in her speech at the “The Next Chapter: Planning for Neurodivergent Lives and Ageing Families” forum here today.
She said disability planning had traditionally focused on early intervention and childhood development, but this needed to be expanded to address the long-term needs of neurodivergent individuals and ageing caregivers.
“Care cannot continue to be treated as an invisible responsibility carried primarily by families, and often by women, without adequate support. It must be recognised as a shared responsibility across families, communities, Government and the wider care ecosystem,” she said.
Nancy said this included specialised care, living arrangements, financial planning, adult support programmes, inclusive environments and social integration, with efforts aligned with the National Plan of Action for Persons with Disabilities 2026-2030, National Plan of Action for Older Persons 2026-2030 and Malaysia Care Strategic Framework and Action Plan 2026-2030.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Healthy Ageing Society (MHAS) president Prof V. Nathan said Malaysia needed comprehensive national information on autistic children, adults and older people to better understand their needs as the population aged.
He said services should move beyond childhood-focused interventions to address access to healthcare, sensory-unfriendly environments, loneliness, mobility difficulties and caregiver stress, while involving neurodivergent people in identifying needs, setting priorities and designing services.
Oasis Place founder Dr Choy Sook Kuen said Malaysia also needed more qualified healthcare and allied health professionals and better-trained family caregivers, including parents, siblings, spouses and other caregivers who provide day-to-day support.
The forum, organised by MHAS in collaboration with Oasis Place, brought together healthcare and social-care professionals, caregivers, advocates and other stakeholders to discuss the long-term needs of neurodivergent adults and families providing lifelong care. — Bernama

Title: Passenger falls onto tracks at Wangsa Maju LRT station after reportedly fainting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — A passenger reportedly fainted before falling onto the tracks at the Wangsa Maju LRT station this morning, causing a brief disruption to services on the Kelana Jaya line.
Rapid KL said the incident occurred at 6.52am.
It said the Platform Intrusion Emergency Stop (PIES) system was activated immediately, cutting power to the tracks as a safety precaution.
“This resulted in a slight delay to Kelana Jaya LRT line services,” it said in a statement posted on its social media channels.
The passenger was rescued from the track area by station personnel and taken to the emergency department for immediate treatment, Rapid KL said.
It advised passengers who feel unwell or require assistance at stations or on platforms to seek help from auxiliary police or station personnel.
Rapid KL also reminded passengers to remain behind the yellow line while waiting for trains.

Title: Bukit Aman: Eight minors, two civil servants among 53 arrested over child sexual abuse materials
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Eight minors aged between 13 and 18 were among dozens arrested for possessing child child sexual abuse materials (CSAM) in a joint operation by Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar told a press conference here that the minors were being investigated for possessing and selling animated CSAM made using artificial intelligence (AI), describing it as a “worrying trend”.
“What is most worrying about this is that among those arrested were minors and civil servants,” he said today.
“This has serious implications and poses a threat to our children,” he added.
Kumar said that the civil servants arrested are a 24-year-old teacher, and a 44-year-old laboratory assistant who works at a different school.
He said the teacher was among 53 of 92 “targets” arrested in a nationwide raid as part of Operation Pedo 3.0, which followed months of investigations.
Only one of those arrested was a foreign national, with the rest being Malaysians, he added.
From the raids, police seized 95 items comprising 90 digital devices such as mobile phones, computers, laptops, tablets, storage devices and routers or modems.
There were also five sex toys confiscated.
“From our initial checks of the devices we found 653,193 digital files, comprising 540,127 child sexual abuse material files and 113,066 adult pornography files,” he said.
Police have opened 52 investigation papers following the operation.
Court action has been taken against 23 while the remaining 29 are still under investigation as of yesterday.

Title: Miti says Bumiputera equity policy is not under its purview but Economy Ministry’s
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) today clarified that it has no information regarding matters related to the Bumiputera equity ownership policy.
Miti said the matter falls under the purview of the Ministry of Economy.
“The ministry hopes that this explanation will help to clarify the ministry’s role on the matter so that the information conveyed to the public is accurate and clear,” it said in a statement today.
The statement was issued following a media statement by the Ministry of Education on Sept 21 regarding the standardisation of ownership requirements for private educational institutions under the ministry. — Bernama

Title: Leatherback makes third Terengganu landing this month, lays 70 eggs
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 22 — The Department of Fisheries Malaysia (DOF), through the Rantau Abang Turtle and Marine Ecosystem Centre (TCIC), recorded three leatherback turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) landings along the Terengganu coast this month, involving 195 eggs that were transferred to a controlled incubation site for protection.
Director-General of Fisheries Datuk Adnan Hussain said the records provide important data to monitor leatherback turtle landings, protect the eggs and improve their survival chances.
The first nesting was recorded at Pasir Putih Beach, Marang, on Sept 1, involving 44 eggs, followed by 81 eggs at Rantau Abang Beach on Sept 13 and 70 eggs at Kuala Abang Beach today.
He said conservation officers successfully located and measured the nesting mother turtle during the third landing at Kuala Abang Beach at about 2am today.
The turtle measured 215 centimetres in carapace length and 115 centimetres in width.
Staff transferred all 70 eggs to the TCIC incubation site at about 6am and reburied them at a depth of 80 to 100 centimetres to replicate natural nesting conditions.
“The incubation period is expected to last between 55 and 70 days, depending on sand temperature, with TCIC conducting periodic monitoring of the nest conditions,” he said in a statement today.
Adnan said sustained conservation efforts, including scientific monitoring, nest management, enforcement and public awareness, as well as cooperation from local communities and fishermen, were crucial to protecting the species.
He urged the public not to disturb or touch sea turtles coming ashore but to immediately report sightings to the DOF for appropriate action.
The DOF also reminded the public that sea turtles and their eggs are protected under relevant laws.
Under the Terengganu Turtle Enactment 1951 (Amendment 2021), offences involving the possession or sale of eggs, or disturbance of sea turtles, carry fines of between RM50,000 and RM250,000 and imprisonment of up to one year, or both, upon conviction.
The department also called on fishing communities, local residents and the public to report any sea turtle landings or sightings to facilitate timely protection and conservation measures. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan investment manager loses RM1.2m in savings and jewellery after scammers spoof police phone number
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — A company investment manager lost about RM1.2 million after she was duped by a scam syndicate through a phone call in Kota Bharu last July.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the woman, a single mother in her 50s, received a call from an individual posing as an authority and claiming that she was involved in a money laundering case.
He said the woman, fearing the consequences, followed the suspect’s instructions, withdrawing money from her bank accounts, including her Employees Provident Fund (EPF) savings, and pawning and selling jewellery worth nearly RM500,000.
“Most concerningly, the woman took about two months before lodging a police report, after all her money had been withdrawn and handed over to the perpetrators.
“She knew that she was not involved in money laundering, but because she was so frightened, she did not tell her family members or the police,” he said in a press conference after the monthly assembly at the Kelantan contingent police headquarters here today.
Mohd Yusoff said the syndicate also used application spoofing technology to make the phone number appear as though the call was from the police, including using the Kelantan IPK’s telephone number.
He said police detected about 68 calls a day using the Kelantan IPK’s number, and the matter was now under investigation.
“Neither the police nor agencies such as Bank Negara Malaysia will call members of the public and instruct them to withdraw money or open a new account.
“If you receive such a call, hang up and contact the relevant agency through its official channels to verify the matter,” he said.
He said police had also sought assistance from Bukit Aman to track down individuals believed to be involved in the scam.
He said the incident began about two months ago before a report was lodged recently and, as of this year, the case was among those involving the largest individual losses recorded in Kelantan.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusoff said Kelantan police would intensify awareness campaigns through the media to curb commercial crime, which continued to show an increase year-on-year. — Bernama

Title: Uncle remanded seven days over death of five-year-old girl allegedly thrown into Johor river
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 22 — A 37-year-old man who allegedly threw his five-year-old niece into a river in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili here, causing her death yesterday, has been remanded for seven days to assist in the investigation.
Sessions Court Judge Hafizah Abdul Rajak granted the police’s remand application until September 28 to facilitate investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
The suspect, who had been receiving treatment at Kota Tinggi Hospital, arrived at the court complex at 9am today, escorted by policemen.
It was reported yesterday that police arrested a local man for allegedly throwing his niece into a river, resulting in her death.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report at about 9.30am before arresting the suspect.
The suspect, who was also the deceased girl’s uncle, allegedly threw the victim into the river before going on a rampage while armed with a machete and chasing the victim’s 40-year-old father.
A police officer was also injured during a struggle while attempting to apprehend the suspect.
Police are still investigating the motive behind the incident, while the suspect is believed to have mental health issues.
The victim’s body was sent to Pasir Gudang Hospital and is expected to be buried in Kampung Sayang here after the post-mortem examination is completed.

Title: Beyond minimum wage, Malaysia needs clearer wage ladders tied to productivity, says Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 22 — Wage compression is hindering working Malaysians from receiving proper compensation despite the narrowing wage gap between low- and semi-skilled workers in Malaysia, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
Citing a recent Bank Negara report, Akmal Nasrullah said the wage difference between low- and semi-skilled workers had narrowed from RM550 in 2016 to RM396 in 2024.
“This means the wage is moving (upwards) at the minimum wage level but comparatively, it is not progressing as well in the successive levels,” he said during the ministry’s monthly assembly at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) today.
As such, he said raising the floor wage was only a starting point and the ministry must develop clearer wage ladders that keep pace with productivity.
Akmal Nasrullah also pointed out that only four states and federal territories had surpassed the national median monthly wage of RM2,940, namely Penang, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
The ministry, he said, had decided to allocate higher development allocations to six states and territories — Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan, Terengganu, Sabah and Sarawak — to support them in also crossing the RM2,940 mark.
While noting that Malaysia’s inflation remained moderate at 1.9 per cent, Akmal Nasrullah said managing cost-of-living pressures was essential for working Malaysians to benefit from salary progressions.
Malaysia last raised the minimum wage from RM1,500 to RM1,700 per month in August 2025 and seeks to scale it up to RM3,000 per month by 2030 under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).

Title: Penang wants more than tourist numbers as it shifts to high-value tourism
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — Penang is seeking the federal government’s support through Budget 2027 to strengthen its tourism agenda, including improving air connectivity, attracting more international events and preserving George Town’s heritage.
State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the priorities were aimed at increasing the value of the tourism sector while ensuring its growth continued to benefit the local economy and community.
He said one of the main priorities was an international air connectivity fund, including matching grants, to attract more direct flights to Penang from strategic markets such as Japan, South Korea, Australia and the Middle East.
“With the Penang International Airport (LTAPP) upgrading project set to double its capacity to 12 million passengers a year, the priority now is to ensure that the capacity can be fully utilised through new routes and increased flight frequencies,” he told Bernama.
The LTAPP expansion and upgrading project is expected to be completed in June 2028, according to reports.
Wong said Penang was also seeking a larger federal matching fund to bid for and attract international conferences, exhibitions, sporting events, festivals, concerts, as well as large-scale arts and cultural events.
He said business events generated an economic impact of about RM1.91 billion last year, demonstrating Penang’s potential to become a major regional hub for business and major events with its new facilities and increased capacity.
The fund could also be used to develop creative content, productions, local festivals and intellectual property that could be brought to the international stage, he said.
Wong also proposed that the government establish a Unesco George Town Conservation and Regeneration Fund to ensure the heritage city continues to thrive as a living heritage city.
He said dedicated allocations were needed for the conservation of heritage buildings, enhancement of public spaces, safety and accessibility, as well as the preservation of traditional businesses, artisans and communities that make George Town a living heritage city.
“We do not want to merely preserve buildings. We need to ensure that the heritage, culture and local communities continue to thrive while being able to generate new economic activities through tourism and the creative economy,” he said.
Wong said Penang’s focus after Visit Malaysia 2026 should shift from pursuing tourist numbers to high-value tourism.
Meanwhile, he called for the formula of channelling 100 per cent of tourism tax to the states in 2026 to be continued next year.
“As Visit Malaysia has been extended to 2027, it is hoped that the 100 per cent allocation of tourism tax can also be continued next year,” he said.
Budget 2027 is expected to be tabled by Prime Minister, who is also Finance Minister, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, on Oct 9. — Bernama

Title: Penang’s Chung Ling high school classroom catches fire, no casualties but 20pc damaged
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — A classroom at SMK(C) Chung Ling in Ayer Itam here caught fire last night, with no casualties reported.
The Penang Fire and Rescue Department said 12 personnel and three fire engines from the Paya Terubong and Lebuh Pantai fire and rescue stations were sent to the school after an emergency call was received at 7.54pm.
“The fire involved a classroom measuring about 20 by 30 square feet, with an estimated 20 per cent damage,” its operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis was quoted as saying by national news agency
Bernama
today.
He said there were no school activities taking place when the fire broke out and no casualties were reported.
The fire was fully extinguished at 8.40pm, after which firefighters carried out further checks to ensure there were no other hazards at the scene.
John said the operation ended at 9.22pm and the case was handed over to the Fire Investigation Team for further action.
He said the cause of the fire and the extent of losses are still under investigation. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan commercial crime losses hit RM33.5m in first eight months of 2026 as scam surge
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — Kelantan recorded losses of RM33.47 million in commercial crime from January to August this year, an increase of RM5.97 million compared with RM27.50 million reported during the same period last year.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the number of commercial crime cases also rose from 1,100 to 1,921, an increase of 821 cases.
He said one of the most significant increases was in e-commerce scams, which rose from 260 to 657 cases, while other cybercrimes also increased from 287 to 444 cases.
“This trend shows that crime is increasingly changing in line with technological developments. Therefore, our actions must also change rapidly, particularly in prevention and public awareness,” he said in his speech at the monthly assembly at the Kelantan contingent police headquarters here yesterday.
However, Mohd Yusoff said the overall crime index for the Kelantan contingent from January to August this year fell three per cent to 1,213 cases compared with 1,251 cases during the same period in 2025.
He said violent crime also declined 11 per cent from 310 to 276 cases, while property crime fell from 941 to 937 cases.
On the drug threat, he said narcotics cases decreased 13 per cent from 18,427 to 16,044 during the period, while arrests fell 10 per cent from 19,469 to 17,579.
He said the value of drugs seized also declined 31.49 per cent from RM25.47 million to RM17.45 million, as a result of more systematic and focused efforts to combat the threat.
In terms of prevention, Mohd Yusoff said the state police continued to implement various approaches, including MPV and URB patrols, AMANITA, community policing programmes and networks with relevant agencies.
He said community participation through the Volunteer Smartphone Patrol (VSP) also needed to be further strengthened, with 150,019 people having registered as VSP members in the Kelantan contingent as of Aug 31.
He said efforts to engage with young people should also take into account the influence of screens, social media and the digital world, which increasingly shape their lives, while maintaining face-to-face interaction to build public trust.
Mohd Yusoff said these ongoing efforts were important to ensure that public safety was always safeguarded, in line with the police’s responsibility to maintain peace in the state. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman denies police MPV escorted cable theft vehicle in Ampang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Police have denied claims circulating online that a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) escorted a vehicle believed to be carrying stolen cables in Kampung Tasik Tambahan, Ampang, last Saturday.
Sinar Harian
reported that Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said police had arrested a cable theft suspect in connection with the incident.
He said claims that the police vehicle was involved in a conspiracy with the cable thieves were untrue.
“The claim that the police vehicle was in collusion with them is untrue.
“The MPV acted based on information from the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters operations room, and the team vehicle also activated its beacon lights in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOP) while carrying out its duties,” he said when contacted by
Sinar Harian
yesterday.
Noor Hisam said the actions of the MPV personnel were in response to a public complaint.
He said one suspect had so far been arrested for further action.
Earlier, closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage from a house near the scene went viral on several social media platforms, including Facebook and Threads.
The footage prompted various reactions from social media users, including claims that the police vehicle had escorted a vehicle believed to be carrying stolen cables.
Noor Hisam’s clarification came after the footage sparked questions over the police vehicle’s presence at the scene and its actions during the incident.

Title: Orang Asli man killed in suspected tiger attack while searching for rotan in Sungai Siput
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — An Orang Asli man was killed after he was believed to have been attacked by a tiger while searching for rotan in a forest area near Kampung Takung, Pos Perwor in Sungai Siput yesterday.
Sinar Harian
reported that Zamberi Angah, 42, was found dead in a bamboo clump near a logging road, about 200 metres from where the attack was believed to have taken place.
Zamberi was believed to have entered the Korbu Forest Reserve with a friend to search for rotan.
The Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) received a report about the incident at about 4.30pm, after which members of its Wildlife Conservation Unit (UKHM) and Sungai Siput Perhilitan personnel rushed to the location, the report said.
A joint search operation began at about 6.30pm involving personnel from the Lintang police station, Civil Defence Force (APM), Civil Volunteer Corps (RELA), as well as about 30 villagers and logging workers.
The Malay daily reported that Zamberi was found at about 6.58pm in a bamboo clump near the logging road.
An inspection at the scene found bite marks on the victim’s neck and signs that parts of his right knee had been eaten up to the waist.
Signs of a struggle, dragging marks, the victim’s blood, tiger paw prints and pieces of his trousers and socks were also found at the scene, according to the report.
The distance between where the attack was believed to have occurred and where Zamberi’s body was found was estimated at about 200 metres.
Lintang assemblyman and Perak Rural Development, Plantation, Agriculture and Food Industry Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Zolkafly Harun also confirmed the incident in a Facebook post yesterday.
He said the incident was deeply distressing and had left a profound impact on the victim’s family and the local community.
“Allahyarham was attacked by a tiger while searching for rotan in the forest with a friend.
“My wife and I also took the time to visit the deceased’s family to convey our condolences and provide a small contribution to help ease the family’s burden,” he was quoted as saying.
He was reported saying that Perhilitan would assist the victim’s family in obtaining the Wildlife Attack Victim Assistance and provide safety advice to residents.
“A tiger trap will be installed in the near future and I hope monitoring and control measures can be carried out immediately to ensure the safety of residents, especially the Orang Asli community who depend on forest resources for their livelihood,” he said.
He also advised the public not to enter the area temporarily, remain vigilant and comply with the authorities’ instructions.

Title: Maritime industry expert seeks Customs dept ruling on RM220m K8 cargoes, calls for industry-wide SOP on petroleum blending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) has been urged to issue a clear written position on the Customs treatment of two petroleum cargoes with a combined declared value exceeding RM220 million, as continued uncertainty could affect shipping agents, terminal operators, cargo owners and other participants in Malaysia’s downstream petroleum sector.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said the company was not asking JKDM to decide the matter in its favour, but to state the applicable law, procedure and documentary requirements in writing.
“This has gone beyond a private commercial disagreement. The industry needs to know whether petroleum cargo declared for transhipment under K8 may be blended or commingled in a Public Licensed Warehouse, what approvals are required, and how the declaration and duty treatment must be handled if the product changes,” he said in a statement today.
The matter concerns two Atlanta Crude Oil cargoes totalling 76,954.325 metric tonnes. The first comprised 34,903.062 tonnes carried by MT Marlin Santorini, while the second comprised 42,051.263 tonnes carried by MT Invictus.
Maritime Network said records reviewed by the company showed that the cargoes were declared under the K8 procedure and discharged into shore tanks at Dialog Terminals Langsat in Johor. The company has asked whether the K8 procedure remained appropriate after the reported blending activity and whether any change in the product’s composition, specifications or tariff classification required a different Customs declaration.
Jeyenderan said Maritime Network had pursued clarification through the proper channels since April, including meetings, formal correspondence, a detailed report submitted in late August, a meeting with officers from JKDM’s Downstream Petroleum Unit on Sept 9 and a further written request sent to the department on the same day.
“After months of emails, meetings, reports and formal letters, the continued absence of a written answer is creating avoidable regulatory uncertainty. A matter involving cargo with a declared value of more than RM220 million should not be left to verbal interpretations,” he said.
He said the latest development was a written response from the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) dated Sept 17.
Based on MIDA’s stated understanding of the arrangement, the cargo owner or client retained ownership of the crude oil, blending components and resulting Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil (VLSFO), while Dialog undertook the blending at its Tanjung Langsat facility and held the relevant Manufacturing Licence.
MIDA said the client was therefore regarded as a trading company and was not required to apply for a Manufacturing Licence for that activity. Crucially, MIDA advised that confirmation on whether the activity could be carried out in a Public Licensed Warehouse and whether duties applied to the process or export of VLSFO should be obtained directly from JKDM because those matters fell under Customs’ purview.
“MIDA has answered the question within its jurisdiction and has expressly identified Customs as the authority for the remaining issues. The matter cannot continue moving from one agency to another. The competent authority is now clear, and what is needed is a written Customs position,” Jeyenderan said.
He said the requested clarification should state whether K8 remained valid where crude oil declared under tariff heading HS 2709.00 was reportedly blended into VLSFO under HS 2710.19, whether K1 or another declaration was required, and what import duty, sales tax, excise duty, export duty or other tax treatment applied.
If no duty or tax was payable, JKDM should identify the relevant exemption, suspension, licence condition or other legal basis, he said.
Maritime Network also called for an industry-wide written guideline or operational standard covering liquid petroleum cargo handled under K8, including rules on blending or commingling, licensed-warehouse conditions, product identity, sampling, tariff classification, mass-balance records and the reconciliation of inbound cargo against the final outgoing export.
Jeyenderan said written guidance would protect both the authorities and the industry by ensuring that the same rules were understood and applied at every Malaysian port and terminal.
“A verbal explanation may depend on the officer present on that day. A written position creates consistency, accountability and equal opportunity. If this activity is permitted, the rules should be transparent and available to every qualified Malaysian industry player. If it is not permitted, the industry must be told clearly so that companies can comply,” he said.
He stressed that the RM220 million figure represented the combined declared value of the two cargoes and was not being presented as an estimate of lost government revenue.
“We are not alleging an offence and we are not asking Customs to prejudge any party. We are asking the authority responsible for Customs law and procedure to close the regulatory gap with a written answer supported by the applicable legal basis,” he said.
Maritime Network said it was prepared to publish or fairly summarise any substantive clarification received from JKDM and correct any factual point shown to be inaccurate.

Title: Education Ministry opens private schools sector to all investors, no more 30pc Bumi rule
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 22 — A minimum of 30 per cent Bumiputera equity ownership is no longer a requirement for private limited companies operating private educational institutions (IPS) under the Ministry of Education (MOE).
The ministry said the decision was reached following discussions with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry.
“This adjustment was made to meet the current needs of the education sector and ensure participation remains open to all parties wishing to contribute to the nation’s educational development,” MOE said in a statement yesterday.
The ministry noted the concerns raised regarding the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for specific IPS owned by private limited companies, as outlined in the IPS Policy Statement Book published in 2006.
It added that it appreciates the contributions of all IPS operators and will continue working with all stakeholders to benefit the education of Malaysian children. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia taps Gulf air links to grow Middle East tourism
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia is strengthening air connectivity and tourism cooperation with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region to boost tourist arrivals from the Middle East.
The effort was highlighted during an official working visit by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture deputy secretary-general (Tourism) Chua Choon Hwa to Dubai from Sept 13 to 17, where he held discussions with airlines, travel agencies and tourism industry players.
According to Tourism Malaysia’s statement today, among the key outcomes were the signing of Memorandums of Understanding between Tourism Malaysia with Emirates and Qatar Airways to strengthen tourism promotion and joint marketing efforts.
Also present was Tourism Malaysia director-general Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim.
During the visit, Chua also met representatives of other airline partners, including Air Arabia, Gulf Air and Etihad Airways, as well as travel agencies and tourism industry players such as Emirates Holidays, Sharaf Travel, Al Rais Travel and Capital Travel.
The engagements also addressed recent changes and the regional situation in the Middle East, which have temporarily affected aviation and tourism activities in the region.
“Air connectivity is fundamental to this effort. By working closely with leading airlines and travel industry partners, we will make Malaysia more accessible to travellers from the UAE, GCC, and the wider Middle Eastern market,” he said.
Additionally, he said Dubai and Abu Dhabi are important international flight hubs, which could also provide greater opportunities for Malaysia to reach markets in Africa and Europe.
According to Tourism Malaysia, Malaysia has welcomed 30,257 visitors from the GCC region from January to June this year, reflecting the market’s potential in family holidays, luxury travel, Muslim-friendly tourism, shopping, wellness, gastronomy, nature and experiential travel.
The initiatives are also in line with the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign, which aims to increase international visitor arrivals, including from the UAE, GCC and wider Middle Eastern markets.
“Tourism Malaysia will continue to leverage partnership and collaborative initiatives with industry alliances to drive sustained growth from the UAE and GCC region,” the statement read. — Bernama

Title: If inflation is falling, why do Malaysians still feel food prices biting hard?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia’s inflation rate is slowing, yet the cost of a meal or a basket of groceries can still feel high for households.
If inflation is falling, why do a plate of nasi lemak, a basket of groceries or a meal at a restaurant still cost more than they did a year or two ago?
When someone says, “It is because of inflation”, what does that actually mean?
Inflation measures how quickly the overall prices of goods and services are rising, rather than whether prices themselves are high or low.
When inflation falls, prices can continue to increase — only at a slower pace.
Take a plate of nasi lemak that costs RM5.
If its price rises to RM5.50 the following year, that is a 10 per cent increase and if it then rises to RM5.61 the year after, the increase is about 2 per cent.
The nasi lemak still costs RM5.61, even though inflation has fallen from 10 per cent to 2 per cent.
What is inflation, how does it affect pricing?
To break it down, inflation is the rate at which the overall prices of goods and services increase over time.
It does not mean every product becomes more expensive by the same amount.
So, when someone says, “It’s inflation,” they are usually referring to a broader rise in prices.
Inflation itself, however, does not explain why a particular item has become more expensive.
For the nasi lemak, we need to look at its ingredients and other costs.
Did ingredients, wages, rent or other operating costs increase?
Those are possible drivers of a price increase, while inflation measures the broader movement across the economy.
If inflation is falling, why do a plate of nasi lemak, a basket of groceries or a meal at a restaurant still cost more than they did a year or two ago? — Picture by Yusof Isa
Prices can still rise
According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), Malaysia’s headline inflation eased from 1.9 per cent in June to 1.8 per cent in July 2026.
The July figures also show why the 1.8 per cent rate should not be interpreted as every item becoming 1.8 per cent more expensive.
For example, DOSM found that 374 of the 573 items in the CPI basket recorded price increases in July, while another 157 items declined, and 42 remained unchanged.
Of the 374 items that increased, 367 recorded increases of 10 per cent or less.
DOSM also reported that annual inflation averaged 1.4 per cent in 2025, down from 1.8 per cent in 2024.
What is getting pricier?
The latest food data shows why it is useful to look beyond the headline figure.
DOSM reported that Food and Beverages inflation increased from 1.4 per cent in June to 1.8 per cent in July 2026, while the group rose 0.3 per cent month-on-month.
Meat prices increased 3.2 per cent year-on-year, with chicken recording a particularly strong increase, from RM10.25 per kg in 2025 to RM10.88 per kg in 2026.
Chicken inflation itself was 6.7 per cent.
As for food away from home, this increased 2.5 per cent, while food at home rose 1.2 per cent.
Other categories recorded smaller increases with fish and other seafood rose 1.1 per cent, fruits and nuts 1.1 per cent, vegetables 1 per cent, and milk and other dairy products and eggs 0.8 per cent.
Cereals and cereal products, as well as oils and fats, each increased 0.2 per cent.
Prices can also fall
Food prices do not always move upwards.
According to DOSM’s annual 2025 data, Food and Beverages inflation was 2.1 per cent, but several food-at-home categories recorded price declines.
Vegetables fell 4.4 per cent, milk and other dairy products and eggs fell 0.9 per cent, while meat and cereals and cereal products each fell 0.3 per cent.
A household buying more chicken or eating out regularly could therefore feel a stronger increase than one buying more vegetables or cereals.
What about our neighbours?
Malaysia’s experience is not unique.
Food prices can remain relatively contained when supply conditions are favourable, although individual items can still rise.
In Indonesia, Bank Indonesia reported that volatile-food inflation eased to 2.52 per cent year-on-year in July 2026, from 5.58 per cent in June.
This is partly due to harvests of chilli varieties and shallots, while also pointing to coordination between the central and regional governments to control food inflation.
Thailand provides another example, whereby its Trade Policy and Strategy Office reported that food and non-alcoholic beverage prices rose 0.98 per cent year-on-year in April 2026.
Prepared food and some fresh vegetables became more expensive, while several fruits and other food items recorded declines.
Harvests, supply, transport costs, global commodity prices and government measures can all affect what consumers pay.
So, what has been happening in Malaysia?
The moderation reflected factors including lower cost pressures and a stronger ringgit, which helped contain the cost of imported goods and inputs.
Bank Negara also pointed to lower global cost pressures and fuel prices as factors that helped keep inflation contained. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Bank Negara also pointed to lower global cost pressures and fuel prices as factors that helped keep inflation contained.
These factors can reduce some of the pressure on businesses and consumers.
However, they do not mean prices have returned to where they were before earlier increases.
Why meals stay expensive
The price of a plate of nasi lemak is not determined only by the cost of rice, coconut milk, anchovies or eggs.
The seller also has to pay for labour, rent, utilities, transportation, packaging and other operating expenses.
So even if the price of one ingredient falls, the final price paid by the customer does not necessarily fall by the same amount.
There can also be a time lag between a change in an input cost and the price consumers see.
Food prices are also influenced by costs beyond the stall or supermarket such as global commodity prices and movements in the ringgit, which can affect domestic costs.
What does it mean for households?
For households, falling inflation means prices are rising more slowly — it does not mean the nasi lemak has returned to RM5.
The price of a plate of nasi lemak cannot be reversed. — Picture by Soo Wern Jun
Falling inflation is not the same as falling prices, and it also does not erase previous price increases.
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) reported that between 2019 and 2024, Malaysia’s headline CPI increased 9.3 per cent, while nominal wages per worker increased by 7.2 per cent.
This does not mean every household experienced those exact changes, instead, it illustrates why households can continue to feel pressure even when the latest inflation rate is relatively low.
A period of lower inflation means prices are not rising as quickly.
So, when the headline inflation rate falls, the question is not simply whether prices are going down, it is also which are rising, which are falling, and whether household incomes are keeping pace.
That is why Malaysians hear inflation is falling yet still feel that their groceries, takeaway meals or favourite nasi lemak are expensive.

Title: ‘This is where we were born’: 9,000 Kampung Bahagia residents wait to rebuild five months after devastating fire
Article:
SANDAKAN, Sept 22 — Where a thousand wooden stilt houses once rose above the water, only blackened ruins remain. The floating village of Kampung Bahagia here was destroyed by a massive fire on April 19, leaving nearly 9,000 residents with nothing but the clothes on their backs.
Against a backdrop of the charred remnants, rows of tents with white canopies — donated by non-governmental organisations — and huts made of plywood line the roadside.
Behind the flimsy walls of those temporary dwellings, some 300 families are struggling to rebuild their lives while awaiting the completion of new housing in the area that had been their “paradise” before the tragedy occurred.
“I now live in a small tent with my seven family members, including three grandchildren. Life without a home is miserable, especially when we have to endure the heat and rain.
“At night, I cannot sleep peacefully because I worry about rain and strong winds. Whenever it rains, we all get wet, and so do our clothes and belongings,” 53-year-old Rohaida Absara told Bernama.
Fire victim Rohaida Absara, 53, repairs her tent after it was torn by strong winds during a recent check on the temporary settlement. — Bernama pic
Glimmer of hope
Rohaida’s family is among the 100 or so families who have been living in the tents since the tragedy, without electricity or a regular supply of clean water.
Whenever dark clouds gather overhead, her anxiety intensifies as she fears the tents could be blown away by strong winds, particularly at night. The families also have to endure scorching daytime heat, as well as the threat of wildlife.
“I never imagined that the house where my family and I had lived for decades would be engulfed by flames and destroyed in the blink of an eye,” she said, her voice filled with sadness.
Simang Damli, 31, who stays in a tent with three other families, said the overcrowded and uncomfortable conditions forced her to send five of her children to stay with relatives, while she remains in the tent with her one-month-old baby.
“Whenever it rains, I take my child to the mosque for shelter as I worry that the canopy will be blown away by the strong wind,” she said.
Simang Damli, 31, shelters in an overcrowded tent with three other families in Sandakan, keeping only her one-month-old baby with her after sending five children to stay with relatives. — Bernama pic
For now, those living in the temporary dwellings depend on water from a nearby hill as well as supplies delivered by water tankers operated by the Sabah Water Department. For electricity, they rely on power sources at the nearby mosque for basic needs such as charging their phones.
Despite the hardships, there is a glimmer of hope for the Kampung Bahagia residents. Bernama was informed that efforts are underway to enable them to rebuild their homes in the village.
Through efforts initiated by the recently formed Kampung Bahagia Village Development and Security Committee (JKKK), the Sabah state government, through the Sabah Lands and Surveys Department (JTU), is actively carrying out site surveying work.
“JTU is currently in the preliminary stage of preparing the site and mapping out the new settlement to facilitate the construction of houses,” said Kampung Bahagia village head Sharif Hashim Sharif Titing.
A view of stilt houses destroyed in a fire at Kampung Bahagia in Sandakan April 19, 2026. — Bernama pic
He said the majority of victims, who are Malaysian citizens, have made their wishes clear: they want to remain in Kampung Bahagia rather than be relocated elsewhere.
For the villagers, the settlement built over the water holds deep sentimental value as their ancestral home and the birthplace of generations of the community.
“The residents very much hope that the community separated by the fire can be reunited on the same site. This is where we were born and where all our memories are kept,” Sharif Hashim said.
He said this is also why residents were willing to stay in temporary structures in nearby areas despite having to live in difficult conditions.
“So far, about 50 tents have been set up by various NGOs, while around 200 small huts have been built by the fire victims themselves on privately owned land with permission (from the owner who has allowed them to reside there temporarily), including my own hut,” he said.
Kampung Bahagia JKKK chairman Mohd Anuar Noah said the committee was formed to monitor the welfare and safety of fire victims sheltering in tents, with personnel conducting night patrols. — Bernama pic
Community spirit
Despite the many shortcomings at the temporary settlement, the spirit of solidarity among Kampung Bahagia residents has remained strong through the establishment of the JKKK.
Its chairman Mohd Anuar Noah said the committee was formed specifically to monitor the welfare and safety of victims sheltering in the tents.
“The residents are exposed to various safety risks, particularly disturbances by animals such as stray dogs that frequently roam the area at night.
“That is why we have personnel conducting night patrols to ensure the tent area remains safe. Thankfully, there have been no untoward incidents so far,” he said.
In terms of health and sanitation, close cooperation among elected representatives, government agencies and NGOs has played an important role in preventing disease outbreaks.
Member of Parliament for Batu Sapi Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan allocated emergency funds for the construction of basic toilets at the site, while Mercy Malaysia is also planning to add two more sanitation units for bathing and washing clothes.
Kampung Bahagia village head Sharif Hashim Sharif Titing said residents want to rebuild on the same site rather than be relocated. — Bernama pic
Solid waste management is carried out regularly by the Sandakan Municipal Council to ensure rubbish is collected on schedule, complemented by residents’ own efforts to organise frequent communal clean-up activities.
Meanwhile, difficulties in obtaining clean water have been eased through water tanker deliveries by the state Water Department at least once every two days, following an official request by the Batu Sapi parliamentary constituency, while residents also share gravity-fed water from a nearby hill.
The concern shown by the country’s top leadership, through Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit with Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor shortly after the tragedy, also provided an early morale boost to the residents.
Financial assistance of RM1,500 for each affected family, RM300 in aid for schoolchildren, as well as free replacement of identification documents have helped ease some of the financial burden borne by the victims.
However, the swift rebuilding of their permanent homes will be the most meaningful step towards healing the wounds of Kampung Bahagia’s 9,000 residents. — Bernama
